articles.title: "It hurt like hell": Travis Kelce speculates he was intentionally hit on injured ankle as Chiefs star questions Falcons tackle
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is not ruling out the possibility that his latest injury scare involved more than an unfortunate tackle.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is not ruling out the possibility that his latest injury scare involved more than an unfortunate tackle. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end was left in pain after taking a hit to his already-injured ankle against the Atlanta Falcons on November 15. Days later, he addressed the incident on his New Heights podcast alongside brother Jason Kelce. While Travis stopped short of accusing anyone of deliberately trying to hurt him, their discussion raised questions about how opponents approach players with known injuries.Travis Kelce questions whether Falcons targeted his injured ankleThe incident briefly forced Kelce out of the Chiefs’ 35-10 victory over Atlanta. DeMarcco Hellams brought him down during the game, and a listener later suggested on the podcast that the Falcons safety had deliberately targeted the ankle because Kelce was already listed with a high-ankle sprain.Travis did not fully dismiss the suggestion, although he made it clear that he could not establish the defender’s intentions.“I don’t know if that was the case; the way he tackled me... and I just got caught in a bad position,” the three-time Super Bowl champion said. “You know, that’s football. And on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional, you know, extra grab and turn of the ankle, you know, it’s just part of it.”He also explained why the tackle felt particularly severe at the time.“I don’t think it was, you know, crazy enough for it to get a flag or it to be a fine or anything like that,” Travis continued. “Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell.”Jason, who knows the physical demands of the NFL from his years with the Philadelphia Eagles, offered another perspective. He said defenders sometimes take advantage of an opponent’s known injury, even without crossing the line into an action that officials would punish.“It’s an interesting point that Kyle is bringing up, because we do know that especially defensive players will target areas that they know are hurt,” the retired Philadelphia Eagles star said.“If they know there’s a knee injury, they’re gonna go low. If they know, like, a quarterback has a specific hand that’s hurt, they might go after the hand. Like, it’s not like bounty gate-type stuff. It’s just like a known thing that happens in the NFL.”Travis Kelce gives Chiefs injury update ahead of Cardinals clashDespite the painful setback, Kelce sounded confident about returning for Kansas City's next game against the Arizona Cardinals on November 22. The veteran tight end acknowledged that playing through a high-ankle sprain makes recovery harder, especially when there is little time to rest between games.“I’m ready to rock and roll this week,” he said. “It’s one of those things where once you turn it in at the beginning of the year, you’ve just got to deal with the high-ankle sprain and the process it takes to heal. When you’re battling through week to week trying to get it to 100%, it’s going to be a lot slower than just taking time off.”Kelce also made clear that his commitment to the team has not changed.“But I love playing this game,” he continued, “and if I’m out there on a good ankle or a bad ankle, it doesn’t matter to me. I’m out there because I love this game. I signed up for this thing to be out there putting my heart on the line and my body on the line for my teammates.”With Kansas City improving to 7-2 after the win over Atlanta, Kelce will be eager to stay on the field as the Chiefs continue their push towards another Super Bowl run. His latest comments have also put fresh attention on the risks players face when opponents know exactly where they are hurting.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New studies indicate possibility of detecting CTE through blood tests, paving way to test for disease in living patients
articles.summary: Currently, CTE can only be detected after someone has died.
articles.body:
With organizations like the NFL and NHL grappling with the prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in former athletes, two new studies may offer a pathway toward overcoming one of the biggest obstacles of the disease: diagnosis.

As of now, CTE can be diagnosed only after death , through direct study and dissection of the brain. However, two studies published this week in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) both point to the possibility of detecting CTE through blood tests.

The first study was published by a research group with the Washington University School of Medicine on Nov. 13; the second , from researchers at Boston University and Banner Health, was published Thursday. Both indicate the presence of biomarkers in the blood that correlate with the presence of CTE.

The Boston University study was conducted in conjunction with the university's CTE Center, which has been at the forefront of researching the impacts of sports and head injuries on the development of CTE. Families of dozens of former NFL and NHL players have had their brains donated to the center for diagnosis and study; more than 100 former NFL players have been posthumously diagnosed with the disease.

While the Washington University study was more general in its relation to CTE, giving it a much larger sample size (229 participants), the BU research focused on the development of CTE in former football players. The study analyzed 21 former players who had previously completed a blood draw before their death and brain donation. Eighteen were found to have CTE, with 16 diagnosed with high-stage CTE; concentrations of the relevant biomarker were higher in the individuals with high-level CTE.

Michael Alosco, the co-director of clinical research at the CTE Center and a co-author of the study, told ESPN that the test was a "game changer" to potentially diagnose CTE in living athletes and patients, though the test appears to only be effective in identifying advanced CTE.

"I'm cautiously optimistic that we can really understand this finding and move it forward in the next five years or so," Alosco said.

In August, a recent study of former players' brains found that at least 25% of them had developed CTE. By October, a different study authored by many of the same researchers indicated that the number was more like 75% after adjusting for selection bias.

At the time of the August study, the NFL issued a statement saying that it encourages players to utilize league resources to address their mental and physical health concerns.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing," the league said.

Boston University's CTE Center appears to be working on multiple methods for detecting CTE in the living: In August, former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck told the Associated Press that he had undergone a series of tests at the university, including a blood draw, cognitive testing and imaging, including an MRI and a PET scan, on his brain.

The families of multiple former NFL and NHL players over the past year have donated brains to labs like the CTE Center, including former lineman Aldon Smith and NHL great Claude Lemieux . Other players, like 24-year-old former defensive end Marshawn Kneeland and Chicago Bears Hall of Famer Steve McMichael were officially diagnosed with CTE after their deaths.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Texans vs. Colts
articles.summary: With Week 11 of the NFL season officially underway, the playoff picture is starting to come together but is far from complete.
articles.body:
With Week 11 of the NFL season officially underway, the playoff picture is starting to come together but is far from complete.

While a handful of teams have established themselves as contenders, there are still plenty of teams in the mix across the board.

After Thursday's matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans, here's a look at where things stand heading into Sunday's games.

Josh Allen and the Bills are still in control of the AFC after picking up a win over the Jets on Sunday, but they could lose their crown in the coming weeks. Buffalo should have no issue against the lowly Dolphins this week, but faces the Chiefs on just four days of rest on Thanksgiving.

The Bengals claimed the AFC North crown from the Steelers with a win last week, and they'll now look to create some more separation.

The Jaguars are in a league of their own in the AFC South and will have a low-stress finish to the season.

The Broncos, Steelers and Browns are all still in the mix, while the Patriots are on the outside looking in after dropping back-to-back games. With Drake Maye potentially out for the season, the defending AFC champions might be done for.

The 49ers have been nearly perfect this season, except for a fluke loss to the Falcons, but their second-half schedule is much tougher than the first half. San Francisco will face the Vikings, Seahawks, Giants and Rams over their next four games, which will be a good litmus test to see whether they're actually contenders or not.

The Lions won their fifth straight last weekend and are starting to look like a serious threat to make a Super Bowl run, but the Kirk Cousins-led Vikings also looked scary in a 30-10 routing of the Packers last week.

Neither the Giants or Panthers have been exactly dominant this year, but they currently have a spot in the playoffs thanks to their weak divisions.

The Seahawks and Rams have both turned things around recently, and it may not be an NFC North-heavy playoff after all. The Cowboys, Commanders, Buccaneers, Saints and Falcons are all still in the mix by virtue of playing in a bad division.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Leads Texans Over Colts, Box Score Stats, Highlights for JT, Jones, Richardson and More
articles.summary: The Houston Texans destroyed the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday evening in an AFC South matchup.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans destroyed the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday evening in an AFC South matchup.

Houston was a 12.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and easily covered thanks in part to quarterback C.J. Stroud's three-touchdown performance and a ferocious defense led by edge-rusher Will Anderson Jr. (four quarterback hits and one sack for a safety).

Texans' C.J. Stroud Says He's Found 'Groove' After Win vs. Colts, 'It's Been Amazing'

Here's a look at a few notable offensive stats. The top fantasy performers (all Texans) included Stroud, wide receivers Nico Collins and Keyson Boutte, tight end Marlin Klein and running back David Montgomery.

On the flip side, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones fell to 1-17 lifetime in primetime games. His lone victory occurred on Dec. 18, 2022, when his former team, the New York Giants, beat the Washington Commanders 20-12.

Backup quarterback Anthony Richardson replaced Jones with 7:51 remaining in regulation, marking the second time he's entered the game in the fourth quarter this season after having done so near the end of the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 1.

The Colts had the upper hand early. Jones led Indianapolis to three points on its first drive after Spencer Shrader's 34-yard field goal, and Colts safety A.J. Haulcy snagged an interception on Houston's first drive, giving Indianapolis the ball on its own 27-yard line.

Indianapolis marched down the field and got into Houston territory before its drive stalled. However, Shrader's 56-yard field goal attempt went wide left.

Stroud soon fired a downfield laser to Collins, who leaped in the air above Colts defensive back Justin Walley for the 42-yard score to go up 6-3 late in the first quarter.

A similar pattern occurred in the second quarter. Stroud fired a great high-arcing pass to Boutte, who went high above Colts CB Kenneth Harris for six. This one was from 24 yards out to cap a 12-play, 85-yard drive. After the PAT, Houston led 14-3 with 7:38 remaining in the first half.

Ka'imi Fairbairn added a 27-yard field goal in the final seconds of the first half to give Houston a 17-3 lead.

The Texans out-gained Indianapolis 202-125 in the first half and earned twice as many first downs (12-6).

Houston continued its dominance in the second half thanks to Anderson, who sacked Jones for a safety to give the Texans a 19-3 lead in the third quarter.

The Texans then engineered a 10-play, 57-yard TD drive. Stroud hit Klein for a 13-yard TD, and the PAT put Houston up 26-3.

Montgomery, who hadn't played since Oct. 11 due to a groin injury, helped grind the clock down in the end. He's all the way back from that Week 5 ailment and amassed 124 yards on 29 touches.

The 4-6 Texans remained alive in the AFC playoff race, although they have work to do and need some help along the way. The 6-4 Cleveland Browns, who beat Houston 27-24 last Sunday and therefore own the head-to-head tiebreaker, currently hold down the AFC's No. 7 playoff seed. Houston will now host the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Meanwhile, the 3-8 Colts have now lost six of their last seven games and are playing out the string of a lost season at this point. They'll return home on Sunday, Nov. 29 to face the Giants.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Week 11 Biggest Takeaways for Every Team
articles.summary: Allow the NFL to distract everyone from playing Grand Theft Auto VI for a bit.
articles.body:
Allow the NFL to distract everyone from playing Grand Theft Auto VI for a bit.

Professional football and video games have long been joined at the hip thanks to the success of Madden NFL. Many of today's NFL players grew up playing Grand Theft Auto and other popular video game franchises.

"I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days," Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Tutu Atwell said in anticipation of the latest GTA release.

However, actual games still needed to be played this weekend. The meeting between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans was marred by poor execution.

The rest of the weekend's action should steal the show, and Bleacher Report analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will break down the biggest stories and most pressing questions emerging from each contest.

How Realistic Are the Playoffs For 4-6 Houston Texans?

The Houston Texans won't go down this season without a fight. After starting the campaign 0-4, they won two in a row before losing two of their next three, including a disheartening defeat to the Cleveland Browns last weekend despite holding a 17-0 halftime lead.

Even so, the Texans took care of business against a talent-deficient Indianapolis Colts squad. At 4-6, Houston owns the same record as the Las Vegas Raiders and Baltimore Ravens coming out of Thursday's contest. Those three squads sit two games behind the AFC's seventh seed, the Cleveland Browns, who are on their bye.

Plus, Houston has winnable games ahead against the Baltimore Ravens, Pittsburgh Steelers and Washington Commanders. Winning all three would put the Texans above .500 with four games remaining.

Will Anderson Jr. Continues to Build Case for Defensive Player of the Year

Will Anderson Jr. entered Thursday's contest with a league-leading 10.5 sacks. He added another against the Colts. This particular quarterback takedown turned out to be his first career safety. The versatile defender also registered two tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.

The Texans' coaching staff allowed Anderson to move around the formation and create mismatches along the Colts' injured offensive front. At the same time, Danielle Hunter wasn't available to take pressure off of Anderson, who faced plenty of chips and double-teams.

Still, Anderson proved to be a game-wrecker once again.

Indianapolis Colts LB CJ Allen Is Silver Lining During Woeful Campaign

The Colts organization was thrilled to land Georgia's CJ Allen in this year's second round. Now, everyone is finally seeing why.

Heavy expectations were placed on the rookie from the very start. He was expected to be the team's starting middle linebacker and wear the green dot as the defensive unit's communicator from Day 1. Unfortunately, injuries derailed Allen's development. But the rookie has started the last four games and he's gotten better with each outing. The stats prove how often he's around the ball.

Allen amassed a game-high 16 total tackles, as well as a tackle for loss, against the Texans. He's now managed 10 or more tackles in three of the last four contests.

The rest of this year's campaign is all about evaluation for the Colts. They appear to have a keeper in the middle of their defense.

What Will It Take for The Colts To Give Anthony Richardson Another Chance?

At this juncture, there's no reason for Daniel Jones to continue starting. The Colts coaching staff should turn to Anthony Richardson and see if the 2023 fourth overall pick can give the offense a boost—and perhaps play well enough to earn another look in 2027.

If the argument is Jones places the Colts in a better position to win, it no longer applies. He has completed less than 60 percent of his passes in seven of his last eight games. He's been a turnover machine this year.

Richardson's superior athleticism could help overcome the team's current shortcomings along the offensive line, and his big arm could make downfield shots a little more realistic.

Without a first-round pick, the Colts aren't incentivized to lose. However, Richardson's evaluation should be at the forefront to better understand what direction the organization must go at quarterback once the offseason begins.

Sunday's action should build to a prime-time crescendo, with the day's final two matchups featuring division leaders.

The New York Giants will host the Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Minnesota Vikings travel to San Francisco to face the 49ers. Both games pit teams with stopgap quarterbacks—who may be ideal fits for their respective situations—against MVP candidates.

Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (1 p.m.)

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (1 p.m.)

Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (1 p.m.)

Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles (1 p.m.)

Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (4:25 p.m.)

Jacksonville Jaguars at New York Giants (4:25 p.m.)

Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (8:20 p.m.)

Monday Night Football: Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders

The front-runner for the 2026 NFL MVP, Joe Burrow, will be in the spotlight during Monday Night Football .

Obviously, MVP cases can also be made for the Jacksonville Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence, Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen, San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy and even the Detroit Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs. However, Burrow currently leads the NFL in completion percentage, passing yards per game, passing touchdowns, QBR and passer rating.

During the contest, the trio of Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins will be facing the league's 31st pass defense. The Washington Commanders better be prepared for the Bengals' high-flying offense or risk being run off the field.

articles.title: After Thursday's loss, will Colts give Anthony Richardson another real shot?
articles.summary: Daniel Jones struggled again. Will Anthony Richardson get another chance? Or has that ship mostly sailed?
articles.body:
Down 26-3 to the Houston Texans Thursday night , the Colts made a quarterback change, benching Daniel Jones and bringing in Anthony Richardson for mop-up duty in the blowout loss.

The Colts took this approach late in the 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Nov. 1, giving Richardson a few token snaps. It wasn't an evaluation; it was a cup of coffee. That was his last appearance prior to Thursday.

Richardson, 24, has been in limbo for a few years now, a gifted talent in a state of arrested development, playing for a team that doesn't appear too jazzed to get a longer re-examination of a player they drafted fourth overall just three years ago.

On Thursday, Richardson entered midway through the fourth quarter and missed his first two throws of the night. There was no second series; the Texans ran out the clock. And it almost feels like the Colts are trying to run out the clock on Richardson, Jones, Riley Leonard — all of it.

Head coach Shane Steichen this week said he takes "everything into account" when it comes to the quarterbacks. He added: "Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward."

Asked about a potential QB change after Thursday's loss, Steichen said, "we'll evaluate everything."

Steichen previously has been reluctant to put all the blame on Jones, and it's fair to point out that the Colts offloaded two notable talents at the trade deadline in offensive guard Quenton Nelson and wide receiver Josh Downs.

But the problems have been chronic, even when those player were on the roster. Jones hasn't had more touchdowns than interceptions in any game this season. He's thrown picks in 10 of his 11 games. The contract extension he signed in the offseason is looking more painful, on the books for $46.8 million next season, although it's a deal the Colts can get out of as a post-June 1 cut.

Still, if we're already forecasting the potential end of Jones in Indianapolis, and likely another pivot at quarterback for the franchise, why is Richardson not even a provisional option at this point? Is he that far gone in their eyes?

The excuse for not making a change this week was the Thursday game and the shortened schedule. But it's not as if Richardson hasn't been here for a minute. It's hard to imagine Steichen sees a whole lot of upside in Richardson, or the hook would have come sooner for Jones. Heck, it wouldn't be stunning if Steichen gave Leonard a chance, even over Richardson, at some point.

The Colts declined Richardson's fifth-year option, so the writing has been on the wall for a bit. It's hard not to look back at that 2024 game when Richardson reportedly " needed a breather " as a turning point in Steichen's trust in the QB, even if he ended up bringing Richardson back a few weeks later. Whenever that turning point happened, the trust level just hasn't been there for some time.

Steichen has hinted that a QB change could come, even prior to Thursday night. So there could be an opportunity for someone. There are six games remaining, with the Week 13 bye upcoming.

But isn't Steichen worried about his job? The general manager is already gone, and the owner is watching the operation closely. Outside of a narrow home win over the Dolphins, it hasn't looked very pretty lately. Steichen is going to do what he feels he needs to do to keep his job.

Is there any upside to bringing Jones back next week against the Giants? The Colts might not believe in Richardson, but they could end up helping each other out. If the QB can string a few games together, it helps his chances elsewhere next season. And if the Colts can win a few games, maybe everyone won't lose their jobs.

The big picture isn't pretty, and the Colts still don't have a first-round pick next year, but it's hard to imagine they can't try to squeeze something out of a player who at least has made some energy-generating plays with his legs, even if Richardson's passing metrics haven't been terribly defensible.

Beggars can't be choosers. Jones is playing like a guy who's less than a year removed from an Achilles injury, and the Colts' roster has been gutted. Sure, Leonard is the QB who might have the best chance to return next season, but Richardson has the better talent.

Can he get one more shot to do something in Indy?

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Explains Why Texans Aren't 'Far Away' Amid NFL Playoff Race After Win vs. Colts
articles.summary: The Houston Texans have had a rough start to the season, but quarterback C.J. Stroud believes the playoffs are still realistic.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans have had a rough start to the season, but quarterback C.J. Stroud believes the playoffs are still realistic.

It's just a matter of finishing strong in close games.

"We're not far away. We've been playing a lot of great teams and we've been close, but close doesn't count in this league," Stroud said on Prime Video's broadcast. "You've gotta go win games and finish tight games at the end. I think we can do a better job of that. That's something we can learn from."

Texans' C.J. Stroud Says He's Found 'Groove' After Win vs. Colts, 'It's Been Amazing'

The Texans took a step in the right direction on Thursday with a 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts, but at 4-6, there's still work to be done.

Houston started the 2025 campaign 3-4 before winning nine straight games. The Texans would need a similar run to get into the postseason this year, and Stroud seems to think they can do it.

articles.title: NFL: CJ Stroud stars as Houston Texans finally win at home this season with 26-3 defeat of Indianapolis Colts
articles.summary: Houston Texans quarterback CJ Stroud throws for 194 yards and three touchdowns in 26-3 win vs Indianapolis Colts; Stroud picked apart Colts side missing injured starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward in first Texans home victory this season
articles.body:
Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns as the Texans used a strong defensive performance to coast to a 26-3 win over the Colts.

With the roof at Reliant Stadium open for the first time since 2024, the Texans won a home game for the first time this season after losing their first four.

"To have a home game win is very good for us and exciting," Stroud said. "I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with."

Stroud picked apart a Colts secondary that was missing injured starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward to help the Texans bounce back from a 27-24 loss to Cleveland last weekend.

It was the third straight game in which Stroud had at least three touchdown passes and the fourth in his last five.

"CJ is producing the way he is producing because of the work he put in throughout the off-season," coach DeMeco Ryans said.

"All of that is paying dividends now. He's been ready for these moments and he's been executing at a high level in these moments."

Stroud gave the Texans a 7-3 lead when he connected with Nico Collins for a 42-yard touchdown late in the first quarter.

Kamari Lassiter intercepted Daniel Jones on the first play of the second quarter. The Texans (4-6) then capped a 12-play, 85-yard drive with a 24-yard TD reception by Kayshon Boutte to extend their lead to 14-3.

The Texans were up by 14 early in the third when Will Anderson Jr sacked Jones in the end zone for a safety that made it 19-3. Anderson leads the NFL with 11.5 sacks and had two tackles in the game to move into first place with 17.

"Obviously, 51 [Anderson] is a problem," Indianapolis coach Shane Steichen said. "We were trying to have a game plan for wherever he was. We were trying to see if he was going right or left. When he was playing right, he was going left. We were trying to keep it away from him as much as we possibly could."

Stroud found rookie Marlin Klein for a 13-yard TD on the next possession.

Ryans was proud of his team for playing a complete game after the Texans fell apart last Sunday against the Browns, blowing a 17-0 lead.

"It's fulfilling to finally see that happen," he said. "We've been in these games a ton where we were up at half-time and come out in the second half and for whatever reason not finish. So for them to actually see it and go do it, I think it will bode well for them to gain confidence for showing that they can do it."

Jones was 12 of 27 for 144 yards with the interception as the Colts (3-8) lost for the sixth time in seven games. Anthony Richardson took over with about seven minutes left and did not complete either of his passes.

Steichen was asked if Jones will remain the starter. "We'll evaluate everything," he said.

The Colts had their worst offensive performance of the season, finishing with a season-low 167 yards and just 38 yards rushing, which was also their fewest this season. They failed to score a touchdown for the first time since a 24-6 loss to Detroit on November 24, 2024.

"I understand where we are as a team," Jones said. "I understand it's an issue to score three points. We have to be better offensively. I am the quarterback, and so, I am responsible. I have to play better. I know that. That's the job."

Houston's David Montgomery had 26 carries for a season-high 107 yards in his return after missing four games with a groin injury.

articles.title: Puka Nacua: Los Angeles Rams star suspended for personal conduct violation
articles.summary: Puka Nacua is given a three-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, although the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver was already out injured.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has been given a three-game suspension by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy.

In March, the 25-year-old was sued for assault and battery by a woman who says he made an antisemitic statement and bit her on the shoulder on New Year's Eve.

That civil lawsuit is ongoing, with a trial date set for March 2028.

While the NFL did not specify the exact reasoning for the suspension, it said the ruling "stems" from the incident involving Nacua and the woman in 2025.

The NFL's player policy says players found to have engaged in such incidents are subject to discipline "even if the conduct does not result in a criminal conviction".

Nacua's attorney has denied his client made any antisemitic statement, and says the bite was "horseplay".

That incident came two weeks after Nacua performed an antisemitic gesture during a livestream appearance, for which he later apologised.

The NFL has now concluded its investigation and has suspended Nacua while he is already out with knee and toe injuries.

He was placed on injured reserve (IR) last week, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games. He has been suspended without pay so will forfeit $950,000 (£725,000).

According to ESPN, the NFL told Nacua "any further violation of the personal conduct policy... will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league".

Shortly before Nacua was sued in March he entered a holistic care facility , external to "improve his overall behavior in every aspect of his life" and completed a rehab programme before attending the start of the Rams' off-season programme in April.

Nacua has been one of the NFL's best wide receivers since being a fifth-round draft pick in 2023. He is in the final year of his rookie contract so is set to receive a lucrative new deal after this season.

Meanwhile, Marlon Humphrey will not play for the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday after being sent home from the team's practice facility for a derogatory comment about the city.

The 30-year-old cornerback said on his podcast that Baltimore was "best at making criminals" and while the mayor Brandon Scott has acknowledged Humphrey's subsequent apology he invited him to "sit down with me , external and some Baltimoreans".

articles.title: ‘Scary’ Baltimore remark sparks backlash as Ravens star’s wife issues lengthy apology amid Marlon Humphrey controversy
articles.summary: Allie Neuzil, wife of new Ravens lineman Ryan Neuzil, deleted a TikTok video and posted a lengthy apology after calling Baltimore “scary.” She filmed it
articles.body: Allie Neuzil, wife of new Ravens lineman Ryan Neuzil, deleted a TikTok video and posted a lengthy apology after calling Baltimore “scary.” She filmed it on the flight from Atlanta, before she had ever visited. Some viewers called her racist, which she denies. The backlash came days after the Ravens sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home from the facility for saying Baltimore is “best at making criminals.” Ryan Neuzil arrived from the Falcons on trade deadline day. Two controversies about the same city hit the Ravens in one week.Allie Neuzil apologizes for calling Baltimore scaryThe video was a game-day vlog. In it, Neuzil called Baltimore scary and filmed a man on the street who appeared to be under the influence of drugs. Criticism spread quickly. She took the video down and went online to explain herself.Her central point was that she had never been to Baltimore when she posted it. She had only heard warnings from other people. Since arriving, she said, the city has been great and strangers have been kind. She also kept the apology post up on purpose, because she wanted people to see she was owning it.“I am going to clear some things up for people that did not see the video I posted that got deleted. My apologies staying up because I meant every word of it and I think that it’s important to keep that up and make sure people know that you know I am taking accountability for this. I am sorry for what was said and for offending people that clearly people were offended by this so there’s no question about it if answer”‘I posted about me being on the plane coming from Atlanta to Baltimore and I said verbatim because Baltimore is scary that’s what I said I’ve at the I’m in Baltimore now obviously at the point that I posted this I had never been to Baltimore I’d only heard things received warnings from people I didn’t know anything about Baltimore okay now that I’ve been in Baltimore it’s great here everyone’s been extremely kind strangers on the street speaking to me just the nicest people sorry the nicest people ever so that’s also part of why I issued this apology is because everyone here has been genuinely great.”Her response to the racism claimsNeuzil pushed back hard on the racism label. She said race was never part of her post and never her intention. She also rejected the idea that the video bashed the city, saying she spoke positively about joining the Ravens and compared the experience favorably with Atlanta.She also claimed she and her husband received death threats from people who said they would harm them if Ryan did not perform well in Baltimore.“At no point was race ever a part of anything I posted. I didn’t mention anything about race. It was not my intention to make anything about race. Um, I have a lot of people commenting and calling me racist and saying that I posted a video bashing Baltimore, which isn’t true.”Marlon Humphrey’s comment and the Ravens’ responseHumphrey made his remark on his podcast, when he was asked what Baltimore is best at making. He apologized the following day, pointing to his years in the city, the birth of his son there and his investment in it. Then the team sent him home Thursday. ESPN reported he will be inactive Sunday.Mayor Brandon Scott fumed over the comment and said it was offensive to young Black boys.Defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said the team loves Humphrey and respects him, even while disagreeing with the remark. Head coach Jesse Minter kept it brief and said these conversations should stay private for the good of the team.Why the two cases differHumphrey has four Pro Bowl nods and two first-team All-Pro honors, all earned in Baltimore. A longtime face of the franchise speaking about the city carries weight, and the reaction showed it.The Neuzils are newcomers. By her own account, Neuzil judged the city on secondhand warnings and changed her mind after arriving. That is a different problem from a veteran who has called the city home for years. No team discipline has been reported for her, since she is not on the roster. Her cost is reputation, and she is trying to repair it in public.For now, Humphrey sits out Sunday, and the Neuzils are new to a city that has now heard from both camps.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Derrick Henry keeps late grandmother Gladys Henry's memory alive through foundation as NFL star awards $10,000 college scholarship
articles.summary: Derrick Henry has spent years making life difficult for NFL defenders, but his biggest motivation has little to do with football.
articles.body: Derrick Henry has spent years making life difficult for NFL defenders, but his biggest motivation has little to do with football. Behind the Baltimore Ravens running back's remarkable career is the memory of a woman who helped shape his childhood and taught him lessons that extended far beyond the field. His grandmother, Gladys Henry, never got to see the full extent of his success. Yet her influence remains visible in his choices today. Through the Two All Foundation, Henry has turned the values she instilled in him into opportunities for children who need support, carrying her legacy into communities far beyond his hometown.Derrick Henry's grandmother shaped the man behind the NFL starLong before Derrick Henry became one of the NFL's most recognisable running backs, his grandmother played a central role in his life. Gladys Henry stepped in when his parents were still teenagers. His mother, Stacy Veal, was 15, while his father, Derrick Henry Sr., was 16 when he was born. Gladys took responsibility for raising him and gave him the care and stability he needed during his early years.She was more than a caregiver. She became his biggest source of support, taught him discipline and helped him understand the importance of education. Henry has often spoken about the sacrifices she made for the family. Her influence stayed with him as he moved from high school football to the University of Alabama and eventually the professional game.In a 2022 interview with NBC Sports, Henry offered a glimpse into the importance of that relationship. "She’s my rock. Somebody who raised me since I was a little boy." He also explained that Gladys stepped in while his parents were trying to finish school and taught him lessons that he still carries.Her advice was not limited to becoming a successful athlete. She wanted him to build a future that would remain secure even after football ended. That message became especially important when Henry made a promise to complete his college education. He graduated from Alabama in 2018, fulfilling a commitment he had made to the woman who raised him.Gladys died in 2016, but Henry has found meaningful ways to keep her memory close. He even has a portrait tattoo of her on his chest. The tribute is a reminder that his achievements are connected to the sacrifices made long before he entered the NFL.The emotional story behind Derrick Henry's purple suitOne of the clearest examples of Henry's connection with his grandmother came in March 2024, when he joined the Baltimore Ravens. At his introductory press conference, the running back arrived wearing a purple suit. The colour matched his new team's identity, but the choice had a much more personal meaning.It was the same suit he had worn to Gladys' funeral. Purple was her favourite colour, and Henry wanted to honour her as he began another important chapter of his career.Explaining the decision during the press conference, he said, "This is actually the suit I wore to my grandmother's funeral, who raised me. She died in 2016, and [purple] is her favorite color."The suit had been packed away among his belongings while he prepared to move. Henry searched through boxes to find it after learning that he would be introduced as a Ravens player. He could have chosen a new outfit for the occasion, but the old suit carried a memory that no expensive designer clothing could replace.There was another moment that strengthened his belief that his grandmother remained close to him. Gladys loved butterflies. Henry said he often noticed them during practices in Tennessee, but had not seen one around his Texas home for nearly two years. Shortly before signing with Baltimore, a butterfly repeatedly flew around him while he was outside with his daughter.He took the unexpected visit as a comforting reminder of his grandmother. For Henry, joining the Ravens was not just a professional decision. Wearing her favourite colour made the moment feel personal, too.Derrick Henry founded Two All Foundation to honour Gladys HenryHenry's desire to preserve his grandmother's values eventually became the driving force behind the Two All Foundation. The NFL running back established the organisation in her honour, with a mission to give young people a fairer chance at success.The foundation's central belief is that a child's future should not be decided by their family background, financial situation, disability or circumstances. It aims to support adolescents and help them access opportunities that might otherwise remain out of reach.The name is connected to a wider purpose: creating an environment where young people can develop their potential rather than feel limited by the challenges around them. The organisation reflects the qualities Henry admired in Gladys, including her role as a provider, mentor and devoted family member.Its work goes beyond occasional donations. The foundation organises community events in Yulee, Florida, Henry's hometown, where children receive school supplies, bicycles and toys. Its annual Community Day has become an important part of the local calendar. The first 300 children receive backpacks and bikes for the school year, while families can enjoy activities, food and entertainment.The organisation also supports young people in Nashville, Baltimore and Alabama. Its initiatives include back-to-school shopping trips, backpack drives, winter coat donations and holiday giveaways. During the festive season, Henry and his family have also helped foster families, provided Thanksgiving meals and covered outstanding layaway balances for families facing financial pressure.These efforts show how Henry has approached charity as an ongoing responsibility rather than a one-time gesture. He wants children to feel supported throughout the year, especially when their families face difficult circumstances.Derrick Henry's latest scholarship effort carries his grandmother's message forwardHenry's commitment to education has remained a central part of his charitable work. In June 2026, he returned to Yulee for a community event organised through his foundation and awarded a local graduate a $10,000 college scholarship.The gesture brought his personal story full circle. Years earlier, Gladys had encouraged him to complete his education and prepare for a future beyond football. Now, Henry is helping another young person take the next step towards a college degree.For a student preparing to enter higher education, financial assistance can make a major difference. Tuition, books, accommodation and other expenses can place pressure on families. A scholarship can ease some of that burden and allow a graduate to focus on the opportunities ahead.The award also reflects the broader purpose of Two All. Henry knows that talent alone does not guarantee success. Young people need encouragement, resources and people willing to believe in them. His foundation seeks to provide some of that support, particularly for children who may not have access to the same opportunities as others.His work has also earned recognition within the NFL community. In January 2026, Henry was named the NFL Players Association's Week 18 Community MVP for his efforts away from the field.For Henry, however, the most meaningful reward may be seeing young people receive chances that can change the direction of their lives. His grandmother gave him stability, guidance and the confidence to pursue his ambitions. Through Two All, he is trying to offer that same encouragement to others.Football has given Henry fame, records and financial success. But his work through the foundation reveals another part of his legacy. Every scholarship, school supply drive and community event carries a message that Gladys taught him early in life: a person's circumstances should never decide how far they can go. Although she is no longer here to witness his achievements, the values she passed on continue to reach children and families through the work he does today.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Puka Nacua loses only money, the Rams lose nothing new, and the NFL gets to say it acted: Inside a three-game suspension that changes almost nothing on the field
articles.summary: The NFL suspended Rams receiver Puka Nacua for three games on Thursday for violating its personal conduct policy.
articles.body: The NFL suspended Rams receiver Puka Nacua for three games on Thursday for violating its personal conduct policy. He will serve the ban on injured reserve, so he misses no extra football. The league did not say what he did. Nacua goes unpaid for those three weeks and can return December 20 against Dallas. The Rams put him on IR on November 12 with a PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, which already kept him out of the Cardinals game. Green Bay, Kansas City and San Francisco were always going to be games without him.Puka Nacua’s suspension costs him pay, not gamesThe ban took effect immediately. He becomes eligible for reinstatement Monday, December 14, after the Rams play at San Francisco, which lines him up for Week 15. The Rams were on a bye in Week 11, so the first suspended week was an empty slot on the calendar anyway.Money is the one hard cost. He forfeits his game checks for three weeks. The league has not published a figure, so none is guessed here.On the field, the Rams lose nothing they had not already lost.Still, the absence stings in ways the schedule does not show. Nacua averages 102.1 receiving yards per game this season, and his 96.2 career average is the best in NFL history. He drew 24 targets against Buffalo in Week 5, the most for any player in a single game since 2009. Davante Adams gave a preview of life without him, piling up 332 yards in the two games Nacua missed with a hip injury. The Rams went 1-1 in those games. Adams is now working back from a hamstring problem and could return against the Packers.What the league said and what it left outThe NFL did not describe the violation. CBS Sports reported that it appears tied to a civil lawsuit alleging Nacua bit a woman on New Year’s Eve and made an antisemitic remark. The suit also lists assault and battery and gender violence claims. His attorney denies the allegations and has called the case a blackmail attempt.The warning matters more than the games. ESPN reported that the league told Nacua any further violation, including failing the conditions of his diversion program, would bring heavier discipline, up to banishment. That reads like a probation notice.There is one real bite in the ban. Nacua cannot enter team facilities while suspended, so he cannot rehab his knee with Rams staff until it ends. Others have taken the same route, including Daniel Ekuale in 2025 and Sam Williams in 2024.Fans noticed the timing. Many online called it convenient, and Sports Illustrated argued the league rushed to suspend a player who was already out. That is a fair read. A ban that sits on top of an injury looks like discipline on paper and little else. What it means in practice depends on his diversion program, not on three Sundays he would have missed regardless.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How far did Nicolas Cage go to play John Madden? The Oscar winner's transformation reveals everything
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage gained about 25 pounds to play John Madden in Amazon MGM Studios’ new biopic “Madden,” and prosthetics covered the rest of a 60-pound change.
articles.body: Nicolas Cage gained about 25 pounds to play John Madden in Amazon MGM Studios’ new biopic “Madden,” and prosthetics covered the rest of a 60-pound change. The 62-year-old discussed the process at the film’s Nov. 4 premiere. He also studied Madden’s old broadcasts and sideline footage, and admitted he knew little about football before taking the part. Christian Bale plays Raiders owner Al Davis. The film is now streaming on Prime Video. Madden died in December 2021.Nicolas Cage gained 25 pounds and wore prosthetics to play MaddenCage described the method to E! News as a mix of two things. “[It was] sort of a hybrid of gaining weight - I gained about 25 pounds and added some prosthetics to achieve a 60-pound look,” he said. So the real weight gain was well under half of what viewers see on screen.His bigger worry was the face. Heavy prosthetics can flatten an actor’s expressions, and Cage did not want that. He feared ending up with what he called a “frozen mask.” For this role the risk was real. Madden talked with his whole face. Anyone who watched him break down a play knows the grin, the raised eyebrows and the wild arm waves were half the show.The work went beyond the makeup chair. Cage went through old broadcasts, interviews and footage from Oakland Raiders sidelines. He picked up Madden’s speech rhythm and the loud, animated way he made a point.Nicolas Cage had little interest in football before the roleCage did not grow up around the sport. “I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn’t interested in team sports whatsoever,” he told The Hollywood Reporter.On paper, that is an odd fit. Madden’s voice was the background noise of Sunday afternoons for millions of Americans. Cage spent those same years with foreign films and martial arts. Still, coming at Madden from the outside may have helped. He had to learn the man piece by piece, like a viewer meeting him for the first time.Bale adds weight of his own as Al Davis. The two actors last shared a screen in 2001’s “Captain Corelli’s Mandolin.” For Raiders fans, the pairing puts one of the franchise’s most important relationships on film.The history behind it is solid. Madden was 32 when he became Raiders head coach in 1969. He led Oakland to seven division titles and the team’s first Super Bowl win, then retired from coaching at 42. His fame kept growing in the broadcast booth and through the video game that carries his name. Plenty of people who grew up with that game never saw him coach a single down.Nearly five years after his death, “Madden” gives those fans a look at the coach before the TV and the video game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers are looking to extend their record to 8-1 with a victory against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Monday; the team travelled to Colorado last Sunday and have been training at altitude this week: watch the game live on Sky Sports NFL
articles.body:
The 87,523-capacity stadium is situated at an altitude of 7,349 feet, and Kyle Shanahan's side are hoping to gain every advantage to improve on their 8-1 record this season against the Vikings on Monday morning, live on Sky Sports NFL.

Their training facility in Santa Clara, California, is at sea level, and the 49ers travelled to the Air Force Academy in Colorado on Sunday, following their 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys.

Kevin O'Connell's Vikings chose to practise in Minnesota rather than try to adjust to the altitude ahead of time.

The 49ers have historically altered their schedule to account for where games are played. They previously trained at the Air Force Academy four years ago in preparation for a game against Arizona Cardinals in Mexico City.

"One thing I know about our organisation that I really respect is everybody, from the top down, they'll do anything to try to help us get acclimated to whatever adversities or things that we have to face throughout the week," said running back Christian McCaffrey, who went to high school in Highlands Ranch, Colorado, 41 miles north of the Air Force Academy.

"So if we're going to play at altitude, coming here and getting acclimated is part of that. So I appreciate it."

Prior to week one, the 49ers spent a week in Melbourne, Australia, before their season curtain-raiser against Los Angeles Rams, who flew in shortly before the game.

San Francisco beat the Rams 27-7, looking sharper after adjusting to the 19-hour time difference.

"I think it's been nice to be here at practice and get some workouts in, and even just doing meetings and just living here for a week," quarterback Brock Purdy said.

"It's been a real thing that we've had to adjust to, and I'm glad that we're here. I think it's the right move for sure."

A half-speed training session was held on Wednesday, with Raheem Morris walking to the lectern on Thursday as if he was labouring to breathe the Colorado air.

"I'm out of breath right now," San Francisco's defensive coordinator said.

"You won't see the effect obviously into the game, but definitely good to get out here and get used to it."

Wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) returned to practice on Thursday after sitting out Wednesday.

It was Evans' first practice since he left an October 19 win over Washington. He has missed the last three games.

"I thought he looked great," Purdy said. "He looked just like good old Mike from what I've been throwing him all year.

"Obviously, for me, I'm extremely encouraged by it. I'm going to go back, watch the film, see how it all looked. But just my initial thoughts were he looked great out there."

Evans was doing work on the side at the start of Thursday's session and then took part in drills with the receiving corps. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder), safeties Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle) and Siran Neal (foot) and defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle) took part in the open portion of practice.

The only player not in uniform was back-up quarterback Mac Jones, who sat out with an illness.

articles.title: Does C.J. Stroud have a girlfriend? Inside the Texans QB's private love life and his mother's biggest influence
articles.summary: C.J. Stroud has not said he is in a relationship, and nothing credible points to a girlfriend right now.
articles.body: C.J. Stroud has not said he is in a relationship, and nothing credible points to a girlfriend right now. The Houston Texans quarterback talks openly about his family, especially his mother, Kimberly, but he keeps his dating life out of view. Rumors surface, as they do for any young star, yet none has been backed by Stroud or by solid proof. What he has made clear is who shaped him: a mother who raised four children largely alone while his father, Coleridge Bernard Stroud III, was incarcerated.Stroud has not confirmed a girlfriendAsk Stroud about his personal life and you get mostly silence. He rarely names anyone he spends time with away from football. That gap has fed the usual online guesswork, and fans keep asking whether a girlfriend exists.As of November 2026, nobody outside his circle can say for sure, and Stroud has not offered an answer. No public confirmation. No named partner. A few rumors have floated around, but none is strong enough to report as fact.It is a sharp contrast with how he handles family. On his mother, he will talk as long as anyone asks.Kimberly Stroud raised four children mostly on her ownKimberly raised C.J. and his three siblings largely by herself after his father went to prison. She worked to keep the household running, and her son has never played it down.At the 2023 NFL Draft, Stroud put it in plain terms. “My mom, she had to play both roles for me for a while: mother and father,” he said. “I’m super blessed to have a mother like I do.”Kimberly has been just as open about him. In a Sports Illustrated profile, she described the moment that defined his path.“He had a choice when his father went away,” she said. “He was going to let that motivate him and be the best or he was going to succumb to it and become a statistic of a kid whose parent did something they shouldn’t. I sit and I’m amazed at how resilient he is. C.J. is the most amazing human I have ever met.”A foundation built from that storyIn November 2023, mother and son launched the C.J. Stroud Foundation. It supports single mothers, children of incarcerated parents and criminal justice reform. The single-mother focus carries extra weight for Kimberly, who raised four kids and knows the job firsthand.Stroud also runs the Godfidant clothing line. Between football, the foundation and the brand, his schedule is crowded, which may be part of why his private life stays private. That is an observation, not a confirmed reason.What the public record does show is where he spends his visible energy. It goes to his mother and to causes built from what the two of them lived through.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
