articles.title: Every NFL Team's Biggest Unanswered Question for the Second Half
articles.summary: Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is already here, and plenty of the questions that surrounded teams when things kicked off more than two months ago have been answered.
articles.body:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is already here, and plenty of the questions that surrounded teams when things kicked off more than two months ago have been answered.

That said, many are still lingering from summer, while others have emerged over the last 10 weeks.

Buffalo Bills: Do they finally have the right recipe?

The winningest franchise in the NFL this decade has repeatedly fallen short of the Super Bowl and has yet to earn the AFC's No. 1 seed during that span. After major offseason changes, they're all alone atop the AFC following an 8-1 start. The critical question is whether they've finally put the right staff and supporting cast around Josh Allen to lock down that first-round bye and make a Super Bowl run.

Miami Dolphins: Which young players can establish themselves as real building blocks for the rebuild?

The new regime will certainly have rope beyond this lost season, and unfortunately they can't currently get more of a gauge on Malik Willis' potential while he's on injured reserve. So we're left with the future everywhere else, with spotlights on guys like Kenneth Grant, Michael Taaffe, Jason Marshall Jr., Dante Trader Jr., Jonah Savaiinaea, Will Kacmarek, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman.

New England Patriots: How do they stay afloat in the playoff race without Drake Maye?

This was already a turnover-happy team that lacked consistency, and now they'll be operating with Tommy DeVito at the helm for the foreseeable future. They'll realistically have to find a way to wrestle a wild-card spot away from Cleveland, Las Vegas, Baltimore and Houston. But if Maye isn't going to return, is there much point in pushing?

New York Jets: When do they turn things over to Cade Klubnik?

Geno Smith has not been the problem for this team, but at 2-8, this season is lost. Why stick with a 36-year-old bridge when you can get an extended look at what your rookie fourth-round pick can bring to the table? There were some promising moments from Klubnik in place of an injured Smith against Buffalo in Week 10.

Baltimore Ravens: How do they stay afloat in the playoff race without Lamar Jackson?

They find themselves in a similar situation to New England. They're not winning games, but now that it's apparent this won't be "the year," do they even want to? Jackson could still return, so they might not want to throw in the towel just yet. But does anyone believe Jacoby Brissett can suddenly reverse this free fall?

Cincinnati Bengals: Are they too one-dimensional?

That three-headed monster at the skill positions is dominating the league right now, but Chase Brown is averaging fewer than 4.0 yards per carry and the rushing offense ranks 22nd in EPA per play. The schedule remains pretty soft the rest of the season, but will talented and well-prepared playoff opponents exploit that lack of balance?

Cleveland Browns: Is this a legitimate playoff team?

They weren't supposed to be, but at 6-4 that last wild-card spot belongs to them. And with Baltimore and New England down starting quarterbacks, the path is pretty clear despite the fact they're the sixth-lowest-scoring team in the NFL. Now we'll see how a very young team handles that reality beyond its Week 11 bye, and whether its defense can keep bailing out an offense that rarely clears 20 points.

Pittsburgh Steelers: What, if anything, gives this team a higher ceiling?

In 2023, 2024 and 2025, they went 10-7 and were defeated handily in the wild-card round each time. Considering Aaron Rodgers' age and lack of weapons, does this team feel any different? Are a new (old) head coach and a seemingly rejuvenated T.J. Watt enough to make them more than one-and-done?

Houston Texans: Can it all finally align?

Last year, C.J. Stroud was the problem. This year, it's been the lack of a running game combined with surprisingly poor defensive play, despite Houston's abundance of talent on that side of the ball. It's wild that Stroud was the league's sixth-highest-rated passer through 10 weeks and Will Anderson Jr. is the favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year, yet the Texans remain below .500. Thursday's 26-3 win over Indianapolis offered a glimpse of a more complete team: The defense allowed just 167 yards, and David Montgomery rushed for 107. But can Houston sustain that balance—and has the turnaround come too late?

Indianapolis Colts: When do they turn to Riley Leonard or Anthony Richardson?

The pre-deadline fire sale made it obvious the Colts know this is a lost season, but they're still sending Daniel Jones out there even though the 29-year-old entered Week 11 as the league's lowest-rated qualified passer. They may want to confirm Jones isn't the guy before auditioning another option, but Richardson is an impending unrestricted free agent. If they're going to give him another look, it's now or likely never.

Jacksonville Jaguars: Can Trevor Lawrence string together a complete elite season?

Lawrence was Mr. Inconsistency in his first four seasons before finding a new level once he settled in with Liam Coen in 2025. If you combine his hot second half last year with his hot first half this year, he's put up 36 touchdown passes to six interceptions for a 113.0 passer rating in his last 15 games. If this truly is the new Trevor Lawrence, the Jags have a good shot at making their first-ever Super Bowl run.

Tennessee Titans: Can they confidently enter the offseason with Cam Ward as the only viable option under center?

In other words, do the Titans need to bring in competition next spring? Ward has picked his game up by completing 68.4 percent of his passes and posting a 98.9 passer rating over the last two weeks, but we've seen those short glimpses before. He may need to continue on that trajectory to avoid a battle for his job in 2027.

Power Ranking Potential 2027 NFL Head Coach Openings

Denver Broncos: Is this model sustainable?

The Broncos lead the division at 7-2, but their plus-12 point differential ranks behind those of the 4-6 Texans and 3-6 Buccaneers. They're 6-0 in one-score games, and the comeback kings of the league. This is the NFL's 30th-ranked total offense! Can they keep winning under these circumstances? It doesn't seem likely, but keep in mind that a similar model got them so close to the Super Bowl last year.

Kansas City Chiefs: Can they survive the toughest remaining schedule among AFC contenders?

In the conference, only the 1-8 Dolphins have a more difficult schedule than the Chiefs down the stretch, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Patrick Mahomes appears to be all the way back, and the Chiefs look like a prime contender again. Still, they're stuck behind Denver in the division and soon face a three-game road trip from hell against the Bills, Rams and Bengals, immediately followed by matchups with New England and San Francisco. Meanwhile, by the same metric, the Broncos have the easiest remaining slate in the league.

Las Vegas Raiders: Who will be a part of the core around Fernando Mendoza in 2027?

Brock Bowers, Kolton Miller, Tyler Linderbaum, Tre Tucker. Cool. Anyone else? Notice I didn't list Ashton Jeanty? It may be a little dramatic, as he's still one of the best receiving backs in the league, but his 3.1 yards-per-attempt average ranks 44th among 46 qualified players. Rookie Mike Washington Jr. has flashed but is also averaging fewer than 4.0 yards per carry, and it's fair to wonder about the rest of the offensive line and receiving corps. They need answers before deciding how to approach this offseason.

Los Angeles Chargers: Can Mike McDaniel save his job?

Heads will have to roll if the 1-8 Chargers don't go on an improbable run down the stretch, and lucrative contracts belonging to Jim Harbaugh and Justin Herbert likely mean the head coach and quarterback are safe through at least 2027. That could leave the new offensive coordinator holding the title of former offensive coordinator before spring arrives unless the league's lowest-scoring offense turns it around soon.

Dallas Cowboys: Is there any hope for this defense?

A unit that ranks 31st in EPA allowed per play, 30th in points allowed per game and 32nd in total defense must turn it around soon, or the Cowboys will be done by January no matter how productive the offense continues to be. Is it possible? They aren't trending in the right direction following an embarrassing performance against San Francisco, but they have a soft homestand the next two weeks before road games against the Seahawks and Rams on either side of their Week 14 bye.

New York Giants: Is J.J. McCarthy a legit threat to Jaxson Dart?

It's early in his tenure with the team, but a fresh setting has seemingly brought out the best in McCarthy following a brutal run in Minnesota. What if he keeps rolling like this and leads the Giants to the playoffs? And what if, by chance, Dart returns for those playoffs? You'd have to stick with McCarthy, right? It could get awkward well before the offseason arrives.

Philadelphia Eagles: Why is the defense toothless?

The majority of the injury damage has occurred on offense, which explains why the Eagles are playing out the string with a 2-7 record. But Vic Fangio's defense has also been a huge problem, highlighted by a league-low five takeaways in nine games. The pass rush has not delivered, nor has a talented secondary. If that doesn't change soon, Fangio could be next to go as the reset continues.

Washington Commanders: Will Jayden Daniels, an opportunistic defense and a soft schedule in a weak division save Dan Quinn?

Considering his notable early-season errors as the Commanders started 1-4-1, many considered Quinn to be a dead coach walking at the team's Week 7 bye. And yet, Washington is right in the thick of things in the wide-open NFC East after a critical Week 10 road victory over the Giants. Daniels hasn't been a consistent plus this year, but he hadn't thrown an interception all season until Week 10. Meanwhile, Quinn's D has improved markedly, generating multiple takeaways in six of its last seven games. Could they actually pull this off?

Chicago Bears: When it matters most, can Caleb Williams avoid whatever happened in Week 9?

The young franchise quarterback threw four interceptions in a game the Bears somehow managed to win. It helped that they were hosting the Buccaneers, but there's no way he'd get away with that against a fellow NFC heavyweight down the stretch or in January. He and that offense will need to work on how they limit and handle pressure moving forward. It'll be interesting to see what changes might have been made during the bye.

Detroit Lions: Can they make a run without Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell?

This one's obvious. A couple of weeks after they lost arguably their second-most important defensive player to a major injury, they lost their undisputed defensive MVP in Week 10. Now, a team in a stacked division that was already a liability on that side of the ball is in an extremely tough spot as its Super Bowl window continues to close. A lot will fall on Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams in particular, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard will have to get creative.

Green Bay Packers: Can Micah Parsons put them over the top?

The Packers defense has actually hung in there without its best player. That unit ranks eighth in EPA allowed per play and has generated the league's second-most takeaways (20). Still, if the Packers are going to overtake the other three bullies in this division, they'll likely need a boost from Parsons, who appears set to return from a torn ACL after the team's Week 11 bye.

Minnesota Vikings: Is Kirk Cousins really the solution?

The Vikings may have the best defense in the NFL, but it was hard to view them as a true contender given their offensive struggles in the first half of the season. The acquisition of Cousins immediately paid dividends when the veteran led the Vikes to 30 points in a critical road victory over the Packers, but the jury is still out on whether he can sustain that.

Atlanta Falcons: Can Michael Penix Jr. prove he's the guy for the job in 2027?

The Falcons are still alive in this punchline of a division, but if they rally back from 3-7 to make the playoffs, we'll likely have an affirmative answer to this question—unless Bijan Robinson does it all on his own. Regardless, Penix has experienced an up-and-down campaign, and he's currently as down as you can be with a 47.7 passer rating in three consecutive losses. If that trend doesn't change soon, the Falcons will enter the offseason without a clue at quarterback.

Carolina Panthers: Can they consistently rely on Bryce Young?

It's the big question we've been asking for nearly four years. We're not much closer to an answer than we were a year ago, which is probably not a great sign considering that he'll be entering his option year in 2027. This team is not a real contender, and Young is not a real franchise quarterback. Will that suddenly change between now and January?

New Orleans Saints: Will Kellen Moore and Tyler Shough remain in their roles beyond 2026?

The improvement just hasn't been there for an offense that ranks 24th in EPA per play and has turned the ball over 14 times in the team's last seven games. It's not all on Shough, who is actually one of the highest-rated passers in the league in the fourth quarter of one-score games, but the sophomore hasn't posted a triple-digit passer rating since September, and there's a growing sense that he may need a fresh mind running that offense.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers: What does Baker Mayfield have left?

It's starting to look as though the 31-year-old peaked in 2023 and 2024. He's currently the league's third-lowest-rated qualified passer, and that rating is 50.1 in his last two games. He's dealing with a foot injury coming out of the team's Week 10 bye, which makes it that much more difficult to believe in a passing offense that ranks 31st in EPA per play. If Mayfield can't get Tampa Bay to the playoffs in this division, the Bucs will really start to regret handing him that lucrative extension in September.

Arizona Cardinals: Can Carson Beck play his way into the 2027 quarterback mix?

At least with Jacoby Brissett now in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew II out for the year, we're getting a long and detailed look at the rookie third-round pick. Beck struggled mightily in his career debut against the Rams last week, but he should get seven more kicks at the can this year.

Los Angeles Rams: Do they have the weapons to survive long absences from Puka Nacua and Davante Adams?

Yes, the Rams have won four consecutive games since losing Adams and won handily without both Adams and Nacua in Week 10, but by the time they take on the Packers following their bye, they won't have played a team with a winning record in six weeks. Their post-bye slate immediately ratchets up with games against Green Bay, Kansas City and San Francisco—all three of which Nacua will miss while on injured reserve. He will also serve a three-game suspension during that stretch, the NFL announced Thursday. Even if Adams makes it back from his hamstring injury early in that span, L.A. could be in trouble if it has to keep leaning heavily on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith.

San Francisco 49ers: Can Nick Bosa get it back to help fuel a Super Bowl run?

The 49ers are somehow 8-1 despite once again being crushed by injuries on both sides of the ball. Still, no storyline looms larger down the stretch than Nick Bosa's struggles with both durability and productivity since returning from last season's torn ACL. After two quiet outings to open 2026, a calf issue sidelined the former Defensive Player of the Year for five straight weeks. Through four appearances overall, he's managed just two quarterback hits and zero sacks. With San Francisco sitting tied for 28th in sacks, the team's championship ceiling may hinge on whether its future Hall of Fame edge rusher can finally flip the switch.

He'll always be a legend in Seattle based on last season's accomplishments, but Darnold has struggled significantly when healthy. And when he's missed action in two separate stints due to injury, backup Drew Lock has put up much better numbers while posting a 4-0 record. Darnold appears to be on track to return from a quad injury following Seattle's Week 11 bye, but a squad that has committed a league-high 44 turnovers since the start of last season can't afford many more flat or sloppy outings from him before its hand is forced.

articles.title: Predicting the Next Big NFL Contract Extensions After Broncos Lock Up Riley Moss
articles.summary: The NFL trade deadline has passed, and the free-agent market is short on starting-caliber talent. However, this doesn't mean that general managers and other personnel executives are just sitting around until the spring.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline has passed, and the free-agent market is short on starting-caliber talent. However, this doesn't mean that general managers and other personnel executives are just sitting around until the spring.

Most franchise decision-makers are hard at work preparing for 2027 and beyond. For many of them, that means working out new contracts with players who have proved themselves to be foundational pieces.

On Thursday, for example, the Denver Broncos locked up standout cornerback Riley Moss with a new four-year, $67 million agreement, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The move comes roughly two weeks after the New York Giants extended cornerback Greg Newsome II on a three-year, $45.8 million deal.

While Moss' deal is the latest in-season extension, it certainly won't be the last. Here, we'll examine seven other players who could sign new deals before the end of the year and how those deals could look, based on factors like positional value, projected role, positional market, and any relevant recent buzz.

Projected Contract Value: Four years, $88 million

Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes has made a habit of extending players early. Had standout safety Brian Branch not suffered a torn Achilles last December, he'd probably already have his second contract.

Presumably, the Lions wanted to see how Branch would respond to the injury and what sort of player he would be following his recovery. While the Alabama product has only been back for four games, Holmes and Co. should have their answer.

Branch has been fantastic since making his return this season. He has started all four games and played 78 percent of Detroit's defensive snaps in those appearances. Since returning, he has recorded 19 total tackles, one tackle for loss, and one interception while allowing an opposing passer rating of only 13.0 in coverage.

Locking up Branch now would make sense for a couple of reasons. For one, the 25-year-old is one of the top players slated to reach 2027 free agency . He plays a premium position and plays it at an elite level.

Secondly, Detroit has a contract stalemate with tight end Sam LaPorta and cannot use the franchise tag on more than one player next spring. Branch's next deal should fall somewhere between those of Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton.

Projected Contract Value: Four years, $76 million

Like Branch, LaPorta suffered a significant injury in 2025 that likely impacted contract discussions during the offseason. The Iowa product suffered a back injury that required surgery and caused him to miss multiple games near the end of the season.

While LaPorta was healthy to begin the 2026 season, he and the Lions couldn't reach an agreement on an extension. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the two sides broke off contract talks in October.

That doesn't mean that Detroit is uninterested in keeping LaPorta long-term. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Lions rebuffed trade interest in LaPorta before the deadline and would still like to work out an extension "eventually."

The question is whether Holmes will wait until the offseason and/or use the franchise tag to keep LaPorta off the open market. If he'd prefer not to use the tag or risk losing his star tight end as a free agent, Holmes may re-open contract discussions before the end of the year.

After all, with 36 receptions for 415 yards and three touchdowns, LaPorta has clearly put last year's injury behind him.

LaPorta should command a contract similar to the four-year, $75 million extension that Tucker Kraft signed in September.

Projected Contract Value: Three years, $78 million

The Seattle Seahawks acquired guard Quenton Nelson shortly before the trade deadline in a deal with the Indianapolis Colts. He only appeared in one game for Seattle before undergoing a " minor procedure " on his knee, though he wasn't placed on injured reserve.

While this could still mean that Nelson only plays in a handful of regular-season games for the Seahawks this year, Seattle probably didn't acquire the eight-time Pro Bowler with the intention of making a short-term investment.

General manager John Schneider sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Indy for Nelson, even though he's in the final year of his contract. One way or another, Schneider likely intends to keep Nelson beyond the 2026 season.

That could mean getting a deal done long before Nelson hits the open market. Seattle will probably want to ensure that he's back to 100 percent before making a long-term offer, but the Seahawks know what they're getting in Nelson.

The 30-year-old has never missed the Pro Bowl and remains one of the top offensive linemen in the league. So far this season, he's ranked first overall among qualifying guards by Pro Football Focus .

Expect Nelson to be paid accordingly and to top Peter Skoronski's market-leading $25-million-per-year contract.

Insider's Take on Pats, Maye Contract Talks

Projected Contract Value: Four years, $104 million

Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract and drew considerable interest at the trade deadline.

However, Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer reported then that Philly was telling teams that Ojomo was unavailable and that another interior defender could be dealt instead.

"The Eagles' reluctance to deal Moro Ojomo, and buzz that they want to eventually sign him long term, has people in the league wondering if they'd eventually trade Jalen Carter," Breer wrote.

Carter, of course, wasn't traded, but Jordan Davis was. This left Ojomo and Carter as the two centerpieces of the Eagles' defensive front, and only one of them is under contract long-term.

General manager Howie Roseman would have found it difficult to extend Ojomo after extending both Davis and Carter during the offseason. With Davis out, locking up Ojomo would be the logical next step.

The 25-year-old has been terrific, even in a largely rotational role. He logged six sacks in 2025 and has logged 62 tackles, 10 tackles for loss, and 33 quarterback pressures since the start of last season.

The $26 million annual salary that Philly was ready to pay Davis should be a good starting price point for Ojomo.

Projected Contract Value: Four years, $220 million

The Houston Texans have not had a great season in 2026. What they have had, though, is a bit of a resurgence by quarterback C.J. Stroud.

Heading into Thursday night, the 25-year-old had thrown 19 touchdown passes with just three interceptions and a career-best 102.4 quarterback rating. He threw for another 194 yards with three touchdowns and an interception against the Indianapolis Colts.

It was important for Houston to see Stroud return to the Pro Bowl level of play he exhibited as a rookie in 2023. While the Texans made the playoffs in each of Stroud's first three seasons, his numbers regressed in 2024 and 2025. Stroud's 2025 campaign ended with a four-interception game against the New England Patriots in the divisional round.

However, the Texans were still happy enough with the Ohio State product to make him an extension offer in the offseason, though they were unable to get a deal done.

"They made a pretty good effort," an unnamed source said, per ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime and Jeremy Fowler .

Houston isn't at risk of losing Stroud in the offseason because it has already exercised the fifth-year option on his rookie contract. Yet, extending him before then would still make a ton of sense.

Stroud is almost certain to use Baker Mayfield's recent $55-million-per-year extension as a starting point in his negotiations. Patrick Mahomes now tops the market with a deal worth $63.1 million annually, but that could change as soon as next year.

Draft picks from 2024 such as Caleb Williams and Drake Maye will become extension-eligible this offseason. While their deals may not surpass Mahomes' in average annual value, they could raise the floor for top-tier quarterback contracts.

Dak Prescott's $60 million annual salary could become the baseline for a new Stroud deal if the Texans wait for the quarterback market to rise again.

Tuli Tuipulotu, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Projected Contract Value: Four years, $92 million

The Los Angeles Chargers didn't win their first game of the 2026 season until Monday. Yet, they largely ignored trade offers at the deadline—though, they did try to send linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos in a deal that eventually fell through.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chargers wanted to avoid "the message of giving up on the season."

That was likely a relevant factor for older veterans on expiring contracts like Khalil Mack. However, in the case of 24-year-old defender Tuli Tuipulotu, the long-term plan probably also played a part.

Tuipulotu is set to be a free agent in 2027, but general manager Joe Hortiz should have no interest in letting him reach the market. The USC product made his first Pro Bowl following a 13-sack 2025 season. While his production has been down this year—along with the efficacy of the entire Los Angeles defense—Tuipulotu has still played at a high level.

Through nine games, Tuipulotu has recorded 32 tackles, three tackles for loss, three sacks, two forced fumbles, an interception and 16 quarterback pressures.

The franchise tag will be an option for L.A., though there's little reason to put a one-year Band-Aid on the situation. Tuipulotu is young, productive, and worthy of a second contract. Expect him to land a deal similar to the four-year, $88 million extension that George Karlaftis signed in 2025.

Parker Washington, WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Contract Value: Four years, $108 million

Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone hasn't been afraid to make bold moves since he took over in 2025. He traded up for cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter in his first draft, and he aggressively added Jordan Davis, Davon Godchaux and Jessie Bates III at the trade deadline.

Extending wide receiver Parker Washington before the end of the season wouldn't necessarily qualify as a bold move, but it would be a wise one.

The 24-year-old Penn State product has established himself as Jacksonville's top receiver over the past two years. He finished last season with 847 receiving yards and five touchdowns, and he's on pace to eclipse those numbers in the coming weeks.

So far this season, Washington has caught 36 passes for 645 yards and six touchdowns. He's set to be a free agent in the offseason, and keeping him away from the open market would be sensible, even if Washington has no real interest in leaving.

"I want to be here," Washington told Action Sports Jax earlier this month.

Money talks, and several teams will be interested in offering it to Washington if he becomes available. Negotiations will probably start in the range of the $25-million-per-year extension that Arizona Cardinals receiver Michael Wilson signed in September.

articles.title: Leonard Williams discusses triumph, adversity, and mission as a champion and father in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Leonard Williams' journey to glory has been long. After enduring countless losing seasons playing for both New York franchises, the former two-time All-American from USC returned to the West Coast to play for a team ready to win. Being traded to Seattle was a blessing, knowing the winning culture the franchise had built over the past decade.
articles.body:
Leonard Williams' journey to glory has been long. After enduring countless losing seasons playing for both New York franchises, the former two-time All-American from USC returned to the West Coast to play for a team ready to win. Being traded to Seattle was a blessing, knowing the winning culture the franchise had built over the past decade.

After narrowly missing the playoffs in 2023 and 2024, the Seahawks won the Super Bowl last year. Williams was at the heart of the NFL's most ferocious defense. While he earned individual accolades with his third Pro Bowl and first second-team All-Pro selection, what mattered most was hoisting the Vince Lombardi trophy. Rather than a specific moment or victory, Williams believes the consistent, collective effort is what made the Seahawks believe they could become champions.

"It was less about one play and more about how we responded week to week," Williams said. "I knew as soon as I got here that this was a special place. By the back half of the season, you could feel it in the locker room. Guys were holding each other accountable. Nobody cared who got the credit for our success. We kept finding ways to win. At some point, you look around the locker room and realize we can do this."

Dominant defensive performances drove those victories. From suffocating the 49ers in back-to-back wins to overwhelming the Patriots in the Super Bowl, Williams left a lasting impact on an extraordinary defense. He believes the cohesiveness and team unity make them a terrifying unit to play against.

"When you play us, it's like welcome to the dark side," Williams laughed. "It's a brotherhood with us. We've got guys at every level who can make plays, but more than that, we play for each other. Everybody runs to the ball and does their job. When eleven guys are flying around with that kind of trust, it's a tough thing to deal with."

Every championship team is led by an empowering coach who knows how to maximize his players. Mike Macdonald has done exactly that in Seattle. In a league where the common belief is that you need an offensive-based head coach to succeed, Macdonald has shown what a highly regarded defensive coach can do in a head coaching role. His influence goes beyond his exceptional scheming and game planning. Williams credits him with his growth and with giving the team the belief that they can be the best.

"Coach puts guys in position to win," Williams stated. "When a coach believes in you like that, you want to go out and give him everything you've got. Seattle has made me more grounded as a player and as a person. A lot of that starts with the culture."

That culture has helped Seattle stay fully connected while battling through adversity this season. Several key players, including Williams, have missed time due to injury. Having a target on your back while being short-handed in games will lead to setbacks as reigning champions. The three-time Pro Bowler remains confident his teammates will keep stepping up and be ready for another championship run.

"Like we've said all along, we have to climb the mountain all over again," Williams said. "What we did last year doesn't give us anything this year. Injuries are part of this game. The next guy up has to be ready. They have been, as our guys have stepped up."

As Williams recovers from a stinger injury, he is staying active off the field. He has collaborated with Dad Gang, a lifestyle brand that embodies fatherhood through apparel. Williams is a proud father of two. He welcomed his first son this year. From growing up fishing with his dad in Florida to wanting to show how much being a father means to him, this was a fantastic opportunity to get involved in something he is deeply passionate about.

"This collab connects on a personal level," Williams stated. "Having my son, Zion, this year changed a lot for me. He's the first thing I think about when I wake up and the last thing before I go to bed. Dad Gang is built by dads, for dads, and that's exactly where I am in life right now. Some of my favorite memories as a kid are being out on the water fishing with my dad. We loved having that quiet time together. That's the kind of stuff I want to pass down to my son."

Twelve years in the NFL have allowed Williams to take on greater responsibility. Coaches look to him for leadership. Players go to him for guidance. Having people count on you builds character over time. As a leader who has faced significant adversity as a professional, he has used it to grow into a composed father who is excited to learn every day.

"Yeah, for sure, football can connect with being a parent," Williams said proudly. "I've dealt with injuries and had some seasons where nothing went our way. Going through all of that taught me patience and how to trust the process, even when you can't see the end of it. Fatherhood is the same way. There's no playbook, you just show up every day and keep growing."

articles.title: Power Ranking Potential 2027 NFL Head Coach Openings Before Any Jobs Are Open
articles.summary: Then it comes to be that the soothing light at the end of your tunnel is just a freight train coming your way.
articles.body:
Then it comes to be that the soothing light at the end of your tunnel is just a freight train coming your way.

Everything is great in the NFL until it isn't. The league prides itself on being the "ultimate meritocracy," but it lacks patience, so losing typically leads to change sooner rather than later.

Last offseason, 10 different franchises changed head coaches. That number will almost certainly be lower this coming offseason, but more turnover will inevitably occur.

Assuming all 10 of those most recent hires will get at least one more season at the helm of their respective teams, and excluding squads currently at .500 or better, we can identify nine organizations that will likely consider a move once the 2026 regular season ends.

Of those nine, four of them—the Dallas Cowboys, Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints and Philadelphia Eagles—are less likely to pull the trigger for varying reasons.

However, the remaining five—Indianapolis Colts, Los Angeles Chargers, New York Jets, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Washington Commanders—are strong candidates to make a move. Among those possibilities, one stands above the rest as the most enticing opportunity.

The Indianapolis Colts are the furthest along among those teams ready for an organizational reset.

General manager Chris Ballard was fired midseason. The franchise already traded away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and skilled slot receiver Josh Downs.

The search for different voices in the building has already begun, but the Colts may be further behind than anyone else about to be mentioned.

None of those outcomes bodes well for head coach Shane Steichen since the team didn't make the postseason during his first three seasons and it owns a 3-14 record since last season's bye in Week 11.

Everything starts at quarterback, of course. The Colts just re-signed Daniel Jones this past offseason. However, the organization can release the veteran signal-caller with a June 1 designation and save $38 million toward the 2027 salary cap, which already includes a projected $78 million in available space.

By removing Jones, Indianapolis is then left without a long-term answer at the game's most important position. To make matters worse, the Colts don't own a first-round pick in next April's draft due to the disastrous Sauce Gardner trade. Thus, the organization has no clear pathway toward acquiring what it believes to be a franchise quarterback.

Maybe the next general manager strikes gold during the event's second day or uses the team's recently acquired extra draft assets to trade into the first round for a quarterback prospect. Otherwise, the Colts will be looking at lesser options, thus placing them at an automatic disadvantage.

To be fair, the rest of Indianapolis' roster still features significant talent.

Three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor remains on the roster. He can either serve as the team's offensive focal point in 2027 or be traded during the spring since he remains the franchise's most valuable piece. Whether or not Taylor is with the team in six months, rookie back Seth McGowan has been impressive spelling the veteran back.

Alec Pierce will return from this year's ankle injury to serve as the team's WR1, which will help the offense drastically. Tyler Warren is one of the game's best young tight ends. Four of the Colts' projected offensive line starters remain under their rookie contracts.

Defensively, a handful of long-term pieces are in place with defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore, defensive end Laiatu Latu, linebacker CJ Allen and possibly safety AJ Haulcy. Plus, cornerbacks Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, as well as safety Cam Bynum, remain signed.

The sins of the past will come back to haunt everyone within the Colts organization. At the same time, the team's roster doesn't require a complete teardown and rebuild.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been nothing but a mediocre franchise since Todd Bowles took over as head coach.

Yes, the Bucs have won three division titles during his tenure and remain in the mix this year as well. However, those results are an indictment of the NFC South more than a feather in Bowles' cap.

Entering Week 11, Tampa Bay owns a 38-39 record since the start of the 2022 campaign.

It's also difficult to see a path toward far more prosperity, and it starts with the organizational decision to extend quarterback Baker Mayfield. The 2018 No. 1 overall pick signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension prior to the start of this season. He's not played well.

Mayfield has always been a streaky passer. When he's confident and letting the ball rip, the Buccaneers quarterback shreds opposing defenses. He's less than two years removed from career highs in completion percentage, passing yardage and passing touchdowns.

At the same time, some may look at Mayfield as damaged goods. A new coach will bring yet another offensive coordinator into the mix. The QB has never had the same coordinator in back-to-back seasons at any point during his professional career. Plus, too many instances can be identified where he tries to do too much and inevitably makes backbreaking mistakes.

Beyond Mayfield, Tampa Bay's best defensive player, Vita Vea, wanted to be traded prior to the start of the season. Plus, significant contributors—including wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr., guard Cody Mauch, tight end Payne Durham and defensive linemen A'Shawn Robinson, Yaya Diaby and Anthony Nelson—are all scheduled to enter free agency after this season.

The team doesn't have significant financial flexibility, either, at least compared to the others mentioned.

Bright spots exist, of course. Specifically, running back Bucky Irving has been outstanding as a workhorse option. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka and left tackle Tristan Wirfs are legitimate building blocks. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter has been taking command of the defense. Antoine Winfield Jr., Tykee Smith, Zyon McCollum, Benjamin Morrison and Jacob Parrish form a solid secondary.

The Buccaneers once had an opportunity to take command of the NFC South during Bowles' tenure. Instead, the roster has slightly deteriorated and/or underperformed over time. Thus, a new philosophy is likely necessary.

Jim Harbaugh's dismissal may be the least likely among those mentioned. At the same time, the Los Angeles Chargers have easily been the league's most disappointing team this fall.

At 1-8, Harbaugh is well on his way to his first losing season as an NFL head coach. In fact, the former NFL quarterback hasn't experienced a non-COVID losing campaign since he led the 2008 Stanford Cardinal to a 5-7 record.

Four issues should make Harbaugh's dismissal a legitimate possibility. Justin Herbert's regression this season has been staggering. Furthermore, Harbaugh hired coordinator Mike McDaniel, who seems to be a terrible fit as the team's offensive play-caller.

An 0–8 start may not serve as the coach's death knell, but even after their first win, a significant turnaround is needed over the final eight games. Also, Harbaugh turns 63 next month. Age shouldn't be a huge factor in the decision, but he's already among the league's five oldest head coaches.

The Chargers remain an intriguing landing spot for another coach based on the same reason Harbaugh wanted it originally: Herbert can be a top-five quarterback when he's playing well.

Obviously, this season is damaging Herbert's reputation. He has previously played at an elite level, though. Another coaching staff should be excited to work with the 28-year-old signal-caller and, hopefully, get him back on track.

Over $100 million in available salary-cap space for 2027 and a possible top-two draft pick make this spot even more intriguing.

Granted, the Chargers' offensive line remains a mess. The team's wide receivers could still use an upgrade. Tuli Tuipulotu, Khalil Mack, Bud Dupree, Dalvin Tomlinson, Daiyan Henley, Troy Dye, Denzel Perryman and Donte Jackson are pending free agents. Plus, injuries always seem to be a problem.

However, this year's severe disappointment may be exactly what the Chargers desperately needed to finally experience legitimate growth next year instead of always falling short of expectations.

Ideal Offseason Landing Spots for NFL QB Reclamation Projects 🛬

NFL Head Coaching Changes That Must Be Made 🏈

Dan Quinn's tenure with the Washington Commanders is trending similarly to his time with the Atlanta Falcons. A strong early performance eventually experiences precipitous decline.

The Commanders may have worked their way to the NFC Championship Game two seasons ago, but the franchise is now well on its way toward back-to-back losing campaigns with five or fewer wins being the benchmark.

Obviously, Quinn and Co. still have a chance to eclipse five wins this fall. Is that good enough to run it back for another season, though?

The most alarming aspect of this year's performance has been the team's complete lack of attention to detail. The squad and its staff have seemed oblivious in certain key situations on more than one occasion. Those mistakes speak to a lack of preparedness. Owner Josh Harris should expect a higher standard from the franchise's on-field product.

Jayden Daniels remains a significant positive for whoever leads the team in 2027. He has dealt with injuries this year and last, which hasn't helped matters. But the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year will be 26 at the start of next season and still operating under his rookie contract.

The Commanders will have their franchise quarterback in place and claim over $90 million of available salary-cap space entering next year's free agency. Washington's brass can frontload deals to entice top names and leave space for Daniels to sign a contract extension later in the process.

Daniels' presence alone will attract top candidates if the Commanders decide to go in another direction. The potential for a quick turnaround doesn't hurt.

Aaron Glenn's process may be unfolding, but a lack of progress in the coach's second season could well be his undoing.

During Glenn's second season as the Detroit Lions' defensive coordinator, the team finished with a 9-8 record. Unless something drastic happens, his New York Jets won't come close to that level of improvement. Currently, New York holds a 2-8 record and it's in the midst of a five-game losing streak.

Jets ownership could easily make the decision to change directions after the current campaign. While that same ownership still holds back this franchise, the Jets are easily the most intriguing opening among the possible vacancies. Four factors work in the team's favor.

First, New York's roster already features significant talent.

Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are a talented running back duo. Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. each bring playmaking skills to wide receiver. Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq may form the league's most naturally gifted tight end tandem. Armand Membou and Olu Fashanu are outstanding offensive tackle bookends.

This year's second overall draft pick, David Bailey, is making a strong case for NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year. Defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. and cornerback D'Angelo Ponds are building blocks as well.

All of this featured talent leads to the second point. The New York Jets entered this season as the youngest team on average among those included.

Most importantly, whoever leads this squad next season will do so with the flexibility of three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft—which likely indicates a new franchise quarterback.

The Jets own a top-four draft pick based on their current record. Even if the organization must still trade up to claim next year's QB1, multiple first-round selections can go a long way to make that happen. As such, any incoming coach will be married to a top prospect from Day 1.

To top it all off, the Jets will have a projected $94 million in available salary-cap space heading into next spring, though some of the team's lump sum will eventually go toward re-signing its young talent.

The Jets could even bring Geno Smith back for another season to serve as a bridge quarterback before handing the reins to whichever first-year signal-caller the front office selects.

Each and every one of these points makes the Jets a desirable landing spot despite the organization's recent history.

articles.title: Travis Kelce opens up about Arrowhead's magic as Chiefs unveil a 70,000-seat, $3 billion stadium in Kansas
articles.summary: For Travis Kelce, Arrowhead Stadium is more than the place where he has built an extraordinary NFL career.
articles.body: For Travis Kelce, Arrowhead Stadium is more than the place where he has built an extraordinary NFL career. It holds years of memories, defining victories and moments that helped shape his life in Kansas City. But the Chiefs tight end is now approaching a major turning point. As Kansas City prepares to move into a new $3 billion stadium in 2031, Kelce has shared what makes his current home so difficult to leave. His emotional connection to Arrowhead comes into focus just as the franchise takes another major step towards its future.Travis Kelce reveals what makes Arrowhead Stadium specialKelce is approaching a rare personal milestone. The Chiefs veteran is set to make his 100th regular-season appearance at Arrowhead when Kansas City faces the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Only three players, Will Shields, Nick Lowery and Dustin Colquitt, have reached that mark for the franchise.The stadium has been part of Kelce's journey since Kansas City selected him in the 2013 NFL Draft. Over the years, it has witnessed his rise from a promising young tight end to one of the greatest players at his position.Speaking to ESPN, Kelce explained why arriving at the stadium still gives him a special feeling."You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere," Kelce said recently during an interview with ESPN."That's the best feeling for me."For Kelce, however, the connection goes beyond the action on the field. He particularly enjoys the atmosphere created by Kansas City's loyal supporters."The fans love to fill that stadium and create those memories and get away from the realities of what the world is," Kelce said. "I just love the fact that they pour so much into it. It just makes you want to play that much harder for them. That definitely makes Arrowhead special."He also highlighted the pregame traditions, especially the tailgating culture and barbecue that bring fans together before kickoff."I like to just feel that feeling of being around the tailgate and the atmosphere," Kelce said. "It's just a part of the ballpark experience. I'm a fan of this game at heart, so getting that feeling of the moment building [before kickoff]. That's all a part of it for me.""Arrowhead's real magic is when you get inside," he added. "It's something I know I'll cherish forever, those moments coming out of the tunnel or just making a big play for [fans] late in the game."Chiefs' $3 billion stadium plans bring a new era closerWhile Kelce continues to celebrate Arrowhead's legacy, the Chiefs are preparing for a different future. The franchise has unveiled fresh renderings of its planned $3 billion domed stadium in Wyandotte County, Kansas.The 70,000-seat venue is expected to open in 2031, following the end of the team's Arrowhead lease after the 2030 season.The proposed development includes restaurants, retail outlets, a team store, a plaza and the Chiefs Hall of Fame. The indoor stadium is also being designed to host events beyond football, including basketball games, the NCAA Final Four and potentially a Super Bowl.Chiefs president Mark Donovan described the announcement as an important moment for the franchise and the state."Today is a historic milestone for the Chiefs and the State of Kansas, and one worth celebrating. The documents before you provide the framework for achieving our shared vision," Donovan said."An extraordinary amount of work brought us here. Now the real work begins: turning that vision into reality and delivering on our commitments."For Kelce, the new stadium could represent the next chapter of the Chiefs' story. But his words make one thing clear: replacing Arrowhead's atmosphere and the memories attached to it will be no easy task.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lions' Aidan Hutchinson Breaks Silence After Knee Injury on Celebration, 'Honestly Can't Believe It'
articles.summary: Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is officially retiring his jumping celebration after suffering a season-ending ACL injury against the New England Patriots on Sunday.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is officially retiring his jumping celebration after suffering a season-ending ACL injury against the New England Patriots on Sunday.

In his first public comments since the injury, Hutchinson wrote on Instagram he "honestly can't believe it" happened because he has jumped on a football field "hundreds of times" over the course of his life.

Skattebo Done with Backflips After Hutch Injury

Hutchinson closed his statement writing it will be the "last time I go airborne" along with a message to his Lions teammates: "Hold down the fort til I'm back, boys."

The play Hutchinson got hurt on was devastating for both teams. It started with him sacking Drake Maye, who left with an ankle injury that could keep him out for the remainder of the season.

Hutchinson got up fine at the end of the play, but did a leaping celebration afterward where his knee buckled. He was diagnosed with a torn ACL that will keep him out for the rest of the season.

A two-time Pro Bowler, Hutchinson is tied for second on the Lions with six sacks this season. He also ranks first on the team with 19 quarterback hits and tied for second with six tackles for loss.

The Lions (7-2) are in a three-way tie with the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears for first place in the NFC North. They will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on Sunday.

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles star Michael Carter II helps new mothers with 15,000 essential supplies as his foundation receives $10,000 recognition
articles.summary: An NFL career can bring fame, money and recognition, but Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Michael Carter II is finding ways to make an impact far beyond the
articles.body: An NFL career can bring fame, money and recognition, but Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Michael Carter II is finding ways to make an impact far beyond the football field. His latest mission focuses on a group that often needs more support than it receives: new and expectant mothers. Through his foundation, Carter has turned a personal experience into a community effort, helping families prepare for parenthood while raising awareness about maternal health. His initiative has already reached hundreds of people and delivered more than 15,000 essential supplies through three events in 2026.Michael Carter II's maternal health initiative reaches families in needCarter's work through the Michael Carter II Foundation has earned recognition from the NFL Players Association. The organisation named him its Week 8 Community MVP after his foundation hosted its third Baby Shower on the Block event on October 20.The Philadelphia gathering welcomed more than 100 community members, including 40 expectant and new mothers and their families. Unlike a traditional baby shower, the event combined celebrations with practical help and healthcare education.Mothers received essential items such as car seats, portable cribs and diapers. They also attended educational sessions covering mental health, prenatal care, maternal healthcare and fatherhood. Carter took part in the fatherhood discussion, highlighting the importance of family support during pregnancy and early childhood.The initiative is part of the foundation's Maternal Health Program, which aims to connect families with healthcare professionals and resources that can make pregnancy and early parenthood less difficult.Carter explained the importance of the work while reacting to his NFLPA recognition."Being named the NFLPA Community MVP means everything to me," Carter said. "Maternal health is not talked about enough, especially in communities where families are already navigating so much. Baby Shower on the Block was about meeting moms where they are -- with real resources, real information and real support. This recognition belongs to every family who showed up and every partner who made it possible."Michael Carter II and wife Alli turn parenthood into a purposeThe cause also has a personal connection for the Eagles defender. Carter and his wife, Alli, have experienced parenthood themselves. Alli works as a labour and delivery nurse, bringing professional experience to their efforts to support mothers.In July, the couple took the initiative to Carter's home state of Georgia. They shared their experiences with parenthood, joined discussions with maternal health experts and donated more than 3,000 diapers to mothers who needed assistance.The foundation was launched in November 2025 with Carter's parents, Donna and Michael Carter Sr. Since then, Baby Shower on the Block has grown into a wider community programme. Across its three events in 2026, the initiative has distributed more than 15,000 supplies to families.The NFLPA also recognised Carter's efforts with a $10,000 donation to his foundation. The honour makes him eligible for the Alan Page Community Award, which carries a $100,000 donation for the winning player's charity.For Carter, the recognition is another step in a mission that reaches beyond football. His work is helping families access resources and reminding new mothers that they do not have to navigate parenthood alone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: As he did with the Giants, Colts QB Daniel Jones is struggling, right after getting paid
articles.summary: Jones was awful again in Thursday night's loss to the Texans.
articles.body:
Daniel Jones' career has had some ups, but also plenty of downs, both with the Giants and with the Colts. He has a knack for having his "ups" in contract years, and his "downs" after getting paid.

Jones was awful in Thursday night's loss to the Texans, continuing the worst season of his career — which comes after the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract in the offseason.

It's not the first time Jones has performed poorly after getting a big deal. In fact, that's all Jones has done throughout his NFL career.

Jones' career started when the Giants made the surprising decision to select him with the sixth overall pick in the 2019 NFL draft. That earned him a four-year, $25.7 million contract, with the Giants having a fifth-year option. Jones didn't live up to expectations on that rookie contract, and was playing some of the worst football of his career when his third season ended early with a neck injury, so the Giants declined his fifth-year option.

But Jones then played very well in his fourth year, leading the Giants to a surprise playoff berth and a win in the wild card round. That led the Giants to sign him to a four-year, $160 million contract in 2023, committing more money to him than his fifth-year option would have cost. Jones responded to that with a fifth season in which he played poorly, suffered another neck injury and then suffered a season-ending torn ACL.

Jones returned in 2024 but was so bad the Giants first benched him, then cut him. Jones spent the rest of that season on the Vikings' practice squad.

In 2025 the Colts signed him to a one-year contract, and he responded by winning a quarterback competition with Anthony Richardson and then playing the best football of his career early in 2025 as the Colts jumped out to an 8-2 start. He started to struggle down the stretch in that season, and then his season was cut short by a torn Achilles tendon, but the Colts were so impressed by his start that they signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract in March.

And now, in the first year of that contract, Jones is worse than ever. His 13 interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the NFL this season and already a career-high, with six more games to play. He's paired that with just seven touchdown passes. He still hasn't had a single game this season with more touchdowns than interceptions. His 65.4 passer rating is a career low. His 30.3 QBR is a career low. His 58.4 percent completion rate is a career low. His 5.6 yards per pass average is a career low. Jones was once an effective runner, but his 2.9 yards per carry average is also a career low. Any way you slice it, Jones is worse than ever.

He's also more expensive than ever. Whether the Colts keep him or cut him, he's going to have a massive salary cap hit in 2027, the kind of cap hit that will make it that much harder for the Colts to rebuild their roster.

If the Colts cut Jones, he may sign another one-year contract with another team. No matter how well he plays, that team would be wise not to give him a lucrative extension.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Wants to Return,  Continue to 'Build on the Legacy'
articles.summary: BEREA,Ohio — Ever since Cleveland Browns owner Jimmy Haslam proclaimed the trade for quarterback Deshaun Watson was a ‘big swing and miss’ at the NFL owners...
articles.body:
BEREA,Ohio — Ever since Cleveland Browns owner Jimmy Haslam proclaimed the trade for quarterback Deshaun Watson was a 'big swing and miss' at the NFL owners meetings in March of 2025, Browns fans had—for the most part—turned the page on the Watson era with the Browns.

Even when Todd Monken was named the Browns newest head coach in January and he declared an open competition between Watson and second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders, most assumed Watson was just going to be phased out being in the final year of his unprecedented contract that paid him $230 million, fully guaranteed. At the time of the trade in March 2022, it was the biggest contract in NFL history and first, fully guaranteed contract. The Browns also gave up six draft choices in the trade, including three first round picks.

Before the 2026 season started, Watson had missed 49 of 68 games with the Browns due to an 11-game suspension from the NFL in 2022 and injuries in 2023-2025, including a broken bone in his throwing shoulder and a twice-ruptured Achilles tendon that sidelined him for all of 2025.

However, Watson was tabbed by Monken after training camp as the starting quarterback after not playing in nearly two seasons and despite a rough start has stuck with him through 10 games.

Even when Watson missed the Saints game after not practicing the week leading up to the game due to a concussion, Monken named Watson the starter for the Texans game, despite Sanders throwing for 297 yards in an overtime loss. Watson rewarded him with a come-from-behind, game-winning drive to give the Browns a 27-24 win and a 6-4 record at the bye.

Watson, 31, has completed 65.1 percent of his passes for 2,118 yards. He is 11th in the NFL in completions, 16th in yardage, seven touchdowns (tied for 26th), four interceptions (tied for fourth-fewest).

His 7.3 yards per attempt is 13th in the NFL and his 89.1 QB rating is 18th in the NFL.

Watson has rushed 59 times for 266 yards and two touchdowns. The nine games that Watson has started in 2026 is the most he has played since joining the Browns.

Despite being inconsistent, Watson has led the Browns to a 6-4 record, including six game-winning drives in the fourth quarter.

Watson's game-winning drive in the final two minutes last week against the Texans was his sixth of the season. He joined Troy Aikman in 1990 and Matthew Stafford in 2016 as the only quarterbacks to lead winning drives in the fourth quarter in each of their team's first six victories. Watson is now tied with Bernie Kosar, who had six game-winning drives in the fourth-quarter in 1986. He is behind only Brian Sipe, who had seven in 1979 for most in a season in franchise history.

On Wednesday of the bye week, Watson was asked if he would want to return to the Browns next season.

"Yeah, of course I want to continue to build on the legacy that I'm building," Watson said after practice. "And again, ultimately, it's up to the front office. It's up to Jimmy (Haslam) and Dee (Haslam). It's up to AB (Andrew Berry). It's up to coach Monken and the city.

"So, at the end of the day, all I can do is continue to play good football, win games, and then, again, let them figure out what they want to do for the future."

Watson was asked if he had any say in the matter.

"That's up to my agent," he said. "That's all David Mulugheta, so I don't even worry about that. Even all the way up to the last game, my future and what that holds is all in God's hands and whoever contacts David.

"So right now, just playing good football, winning games, enjoying this moment because it can all be taken away regardless. So right now I'm just focusing on today, this bye week and then getting back up here and finishing out the season strong."

The Browns traded away reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett with the presumption that adding a second, first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft might help the Browns to acquire the Browns future starting quarterback, if the front office felt there were better options going forward than Watson, Sanders, Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green. Reports have said the Browns front office and personnel team have been scouring college football games this fall looking at top quarterback prospects.

Watson said he is just focusing on the present and trying to continue to improve.

"Again, I'm focused on myself now," Watson said. "Again, I'm not really concerned about any narrative that's going on.

"Yes, awesomeness is definitely cool to have, but at the end of the day, I always knew who I was and I always knew what I was about," he said. "That's why I just block out even the success. I try to stay neutral, just try to stay poised and focus on what really matters and that's just finding ways to get better in my career and making sure that my home and my family and friends are good, and they are."

Obviously, there is a lot of the season that needs to play out with seven games to play, which will determine what the Browns ultimately do, but that the Browns are even in this situation, to consider re-signing Watson is a possibility that is hard to imagine anyone saw coming before the 2026 season began.

articles.title: NFL mock draft: Arizona Cardinals take tackle in Round 1
articles.summary: In a new mock draft from ESPN's Jordan Reid, the Cardinals pass on a quarter back with the seventh overall pick.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals are only 3-7 and right now would have the seventh pick in the 2027 NFL draft. We can defeinitely look ahead to the draft and begin to think about players and positions.

While the quarterback position is one to pay attention to, in a new mock draft by ESPN's Jordan Reid, they don't go with a quarterback.

Instead, they take LSU tackle Jordan Seaton.

The Cardinals desperately need to add help in the trenches, and Seaton is an upper-tier athlete who is very polished in pass protection. He has allowed only one sack and four pressures this season on 344 pass-blocking snaps. He is more than capable of mirroring and matching edge rushers, though he needs to get stronger and improve his anchor and drive strength. But Seaton would be a plug-and-play starting option at either tackle spot opposite Paris Johnson Jr. , who will be on his fifth-year option in 2027.

The Cardinals need help at a lot of positions. That includes tackle. While Johnson will be back next season, right tackle is certainly a position that could be upgraded, as Elijah Wilkinson has manned that spot all year.

To take Seaton, they pass for Notre Dame QB C.J. Carr. Carr is selected one pick later at No. 8 by the Atlanta Falcons.

Would the Cardinals do that? Based on one start by Carson Beck, it seems doubtful, unless they had addressed the quarterback position through free agency or a trade.

With a top-10 pick, the Cardinals should be able to land top talent at a premium position of need. Whether that is a tackle, a quarterback, a pass rusher or cornerback, they could use talent almost anywhere.

articles.title: Nick Wright says one NFL player is sneakily having an MVP level season
articles.summary: Nick Wright has floated the idea that Jaxon Smith-Njigba could be in contention for the 2026 NFL MVP award. The Seattle Seahawks as a team have declined this...
articles.body:
Nick Wright has floated the idea that Jaxon Smith-Njigba could be in contention for the 2026 NFL MVP award.

The Seattle Seahawks as a team have declined this year, already losing four games after going 14-3 en route to the Super Bowl in the previous campaign. But while they have fallen off, Smith-Njigba is still one of the best receivers in the NFL in the current season.

He has the most receiving yards (1,207) of any player by a considerable distance, with CeeDee Lamb (976) second. Jaxon is also leading the league in receiving touchdowns (10) and has the most receptions (79) ahead of the weekend's action.

In turn, it is perhaps not surprising that, when speaking via What's Wright? With Nick Wright this week, Wright shared his opinion that Smith-Njigba could be a sneaky argument for MVP.

He said: "The Lions can just hand the ball to Jahmyr Gibbs. That's not how it works with JSN. And JSN has been doing it with two different quarterbacks, which I think is super impressive. I think JSN sneaky has an MVP argument, like Barnwell talked about. Everybody knows he's the only way they can move the ball, and no one can slow him down."

History suggests Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't be named MVP

While the Seahawks wide receiver is no doubt in great form right now, the NFL has made a habit of only really giving the MVP award to quarterbacks.

In fact, since 2012, running back Adrian Peterson is the only non-quarterback to pick up the prize:

Furthermore, a wide receiver has never actually been named the MVP during the history of the award.

With that in mind, this year's accolade will most likely end up in the hands of someone like Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy or Josh Allen.

articles.title: Texans' C.J. Stroud Says He's Found 'Groove' After Win vs. Colts, 'It's Been Amazing'
articles.summary: C.J. Stroud has spent most of the season on a heater, but even by that standard the Houston Texans quarterback felt great coming out of Thursday's 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
C.J. Stroud has spent most of the season on a heater, but even by that standard the Houston Texans quarterback felt great coming out of Thursday's 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Stroud discussed the "groove" he has been in this season.

"I knew what type of player I could be in this league," Stroud said. "And to just get in that groove and have a rhythm, it's been amazing. Honestly, I would be lying to you if I said it didn't feel good."

Stroud finished 21-of-27 for 194 yards, three touchdowns and one interception to help the Texans bounce back after a disappointing loss to the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

Thursday night was Stroud's third consecutive game with at least three touchdown passes. His four games with at least three touchdown passes is tied for third-most in the NFL, behind only Joe Burrow (six) and Trevor Lawrence (five).

Stroud is one touchdown pass from matching his career-high of 23 set during his rookie season in 2023.

The victory improved Houston's record to 4-6 overall. There is still a path to the playoffs for the Texans, but they will need some help over the final seven weeks of the season because the Browns (6-4) currently hold the last wild card spot and own the head-to-head tiebreaker as a result of last Sunday's win.

articles.title: NFL to hold fifth annual John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration
articles.summary: A special NFL-produced Madden Hallmark will kick off each broadcast conveying what Thanksgiving meant to him
articles.body:
For the fifth year, the National Football League will honor and commemorate the late John Madden with a Thanksgiving Celebration on Thursday, Nov. 26.

Network partners CBS, FOX and NBC will continue to celebrate Madden's contributions to the game, both on the field and in the broadcast booth, with tributes throughout each game on Thanksgiving Day.

A special NFL-produced Madden Hallmark will kick off each broadcast conveying what Thanksgiving meant to him, as he uttered the now famous "There's no place that I would rather be today on Thanksgiving than right here, right now, at a football game."

A special coin featuring a silhouette of Coach Madden on one side ("Heads") and a six-legged turducken on the reverse side ("Tails") will be used for the coin toss, and a patch featuring a silhouette of Coach Madden will be included on the jersey of each player at all three games.

The John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration began in 2022 as a way to honor Madden.

articles.title: Daniel Jones Makes Wrong Kind of NFL History with Rare Stat After Colts' Loss to Texans
articles.summary: It's no secret this has been a disastrous season for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, but Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans put a bright spotlight on it.
articles.body:
It's no secret this has been a disastrous season for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, but Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans put a bright spotlight on it.

Per CBS Sports' Doug Clawson, Jones is the first quarterback in the last 45 years who failed to throw more touchdown passes than interceptions in each of the first 11 games of a season as the starter.

Jones finished 12-of-27 for 144 yards with no touchdowns and one interception against the Texans. He was benched midway through the fourth quarter in favor of Anthony Richardson.

The 29-year-old Jones has the same number of games this season with more interceptions than touchdown passes as he does equal touchdown passes and interceptions (five).

If you go back to last season, Jones' streak of games not having more passing touchdowns than interceptions is at 12. He tore his Achilles in Week 14 last season against the Jacksonville Jaguars, leaving the game with no touchdowns and one interception.

Jones' 13 interceptions this season are two more than any other quarterback in the NFL.

articles.title: Week 11 Waiver-Wire Pickups and Sleepers Available in Majority of Fantasy Leagues
articles.summary: Week 11 got underway with Thursday night's AFC South showdown between the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts. The remaining schedule is a small one, as a whopping six teams are on bye this week.
articles.body:
Week 11 got underway with Thursday night's AFC South showdown between the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts. The remaining schedule is a small one, as a whopping six teams are on bye this week.

The Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks have the week off.

This means that many fantasy managers will be scrambling to fill roster spots before the weekend. While waiver claims have been processed in most leagues, the following sleepers may still be available in yours.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Cam Ward was a popular waiver-wire target early in the week, and he's still only rostered in 28 percent of fantasy leagues. While the Tennessee Titans' struggles may cause many managers to discount the second-year quarterback, he's becoming a terrific streaming option.

The Titans have started to run more of their offense through Ward, who has flashed some legitimate dual-threat ability over the past couple of weeks. He has rushed for at least 39 yards and thrown two touchdown passes in each of his last two games.

Ward has also topped 20 fantasy points in each of his last two outings. He'll have a good chance to keep the streak going this week against a suspect Dallas Cowboys defense.

Dallas gave up 31.7 fantasy points to Brock Purdy last week and has surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season.

San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black doesn't have a great matchup this week, as the Minnesota Vikings have surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs. However, he's one of the only backs who are likely to be available and who are also likely to have a high-floor role.

Black has seen a lot of work as a complement to starter Christian McCaffrey. He has logged at least 11 carries in each of his last three games and has topped 10 fantasy points in two out of the three.

The rookie out of Indiana has also seen a fair bit of work in the passing game, with five targets in his last three outings. This is why he has a reasonable PPR floor, even in a backup role and in a tough matchup.

Black has been heavily targeted but is still rostered in just 42 percent of leagues.

Denver Broncos receiver Pat Bryant came off injured reserve for Week 9 and had a big day against the Carolina Panthers. He finished with four catches for 56 yards and a touchdown on five targets while showing that he is ready to play a significant role.

"All the stuff you guys saw," head coach Sean Payton said, per Kyle Fredrickson of The Denver Gazette . "He was on point during the week."

The Broncos are coming off their bye, and while Jaylen Waddle (concussion) is trending in the right direction, Bryant should still be a part of the game plan. He'll also have a favorable matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders at home.

Las Vegas has surrendered the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing wide receivers this season. Bryant is rostered in just 17 percent of fantasy leagues.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, TE, Washington Commanders

Even with several starting-caliber tight ends on bye this week, Chigoziem Okonkwo remains rostered in only 38 percent of leagues.

The Washington Commanders pass-catcher should play a large role on Monday night against the Cincinnati Bengals. Cincinnati's offense has been on fire, and it will almost certainly leave Washington chasing points through the air.

Okonkwo has been one of Jayden Daniels' more reliable targets this season, especially after the loss of Terry McLaurin to a torn ACL. He delivered a modest 6.4 fantasy points last week, but he was targeted eight times during the win over the New York Giants.

Expect Okonkwo to be targeted early and often against a Cincinnati defense that has been susceptible to opposing tight ends. The Bengals have surrendered the ninth-most fantasy points to the position.
