articles.title: NFL Exploring New Travel Rules for Teams Playing in Future International Games
articles.summary: As team travel plans became a major talking point of the early NFL season for international games, the league could change the rules to require a minimum number of days spent in a location for games played outside the United States.
articles.body:
As team travel plans became a major talking point of the early NFL season for international games, the league could change the rules to require a minimum number of days spent in a location for games played outside the United States.

Peter O'Reilly, NFL executive VP of club business, major events and international, told The Athletic's Jayna Bardahl and Saad Yousuf the league is looking at a potential travel requirement for international games.

"Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at."

Every NFL Team's Biggest Unanswered Question 🤔

O'Reilly also explained one reason for the change is to ensure teams are there for more than just the game because the NFL wants to promote international expansion, which is easier to do in new markets when fans can interact with players and coaches.

"Having access to players and that type of experience when they're in the market does have a lasting impact," O'Reilly said. "That's a factor when you start to think about encouraging or potentially looking at a policy where you'd want a club in the market for more than the day before."

The first international game of the season between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams was centered largely around the travel to Australia for both teams.

San Francisco arrived in Melbourne roughly one week before the Sept. 11 game to get acclimated to the time difference. The Rams left during the week of the game on Tuesday and arrived on Thursday, approximately 24 hours before kickoff.

Rams head coach Sean McVay explained the idea was more of a big-picture one to keep players and coaches on their normal body clock, rather than get acclimated to one routine, then have to reacclimate to their pre-travel routine.

Fox Sports' Bucky Brooks , who previously worked as an analyst for the Jacksonville Jaguars, wrote during the 2025 season that Jacksonville historically travels overseas early in the week for international games.

The Jaguars are perhaps the most well-traveled team as part of the NFL's international series. They have essentially adopted England as a second home, having played 16 games in London since the 2013 season.

This season saw the NFL expand the international series to a record nine games, including the first-ever regular-season games in Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro and Paris.

The NFL's international schedule concludes on Sunday with a marquee matchup between the Minnesota Vikings and 49ers in Mexico City.

articles.title: Jaguars' Udinski, Campanile Eyed as Top NFL HC Candidates by Insider amid Latest Rumors
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars offensive coordinator Grant Udinski and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile are reportedly both making waves as potential head coaching candidates ahead of the next coaching cycle.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars offensive coordinator Grant Udinski and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile are reportedly both making waves as potential head coaching candidates ahead of the next coaching cycle.

Dianna Russini wrote Friday that she "wouldn't be surprised to see one or both get a head job this winter."

Udinski and Campanile were already on the radar as head coaching candidates prior to the 2026 season.

NFL Head Coaching Changes That Must Be Made 🏈

This past offseason, Udinski had head coaching interviews with both the Cleveland Browns and Buffalo Bills, while Campanile interviewed with the Baltimore Ravens, Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals.

Udinski and Campanile have only helped their cases this season to eventually become NFL head coaches, as the Jags are among the top teams in the NFL with a 7-2 record.

The offense, led by Udinski and head coach Liam Coen, ranks ninth in the NFL in total yards per game and fourth in scoring, while Campanile's defense is No. 9 in total defense and No. 2 in scoring defense.

With a top-five offense in points for and a top-five defense in points against, it is no wonder that the Jaguars have the league's best point differential at plus-125.

There is still a lot of season left to be played, and the candidacies of Udinski and Campanile could be impacted by the manner in which the Jags finish the regular season and perform in the playoffs.

However, given how the Jaguars have fared with them in prominent positions over the past two seasons, all signs point toward them being among the most highly sought after coaches available.

Losing both Udinski and Campanile in the same offseason would be a major blow to the Jags as well, which perhaps creates a sense of urgency to win the Super Bowl this season.

That sense of urgency was apparent at the trade deadline when Jacksonville went all in by acquiring safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux.

Those were the moves of an organization that is intent on winning a championship, regardless of what the future holds for Udinski and Campanile.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Has Knee Surgery, Injury Return Timeline Updated by Rams' Sean McVay
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams star Puka Nacua's status for the remainder of the season is unclear after he underwent knee surgery.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star Puka Nacua's status for the remainder of the season is unclear after he underwent knee surgery.

Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Nacua had MCL surgery this week and will be out for "a couple of months."

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the NFL "was unaware" that Nacua had undergone knee surgery when it suspended him for three games.

Nacua injured his knee and toe on the Rams' final offensive play against the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8.

McVay announced the following day Nacua was going on injured reserve after being diagnosed with a sprained MCL, PCL and turf toe.

The IR stint meant Nacua's earliest return date would be prior to Week 15 when the Rams host the Dallas Cowboys, but now the timeline for his comeback could depend on if the team gets into the playoffs and how far they advance.

Nacua was also suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy, but he is being allowed to serve the suspension while on IR.

If Nacua's earliest return timeline is within two months, he could potentially return around Jan. 20. The divisional round will be played over the weekend of Jan. 23-24.

This does seemingly end Nacua's regular season. He has played seven games, recording 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.

There is some good news for the Rams on the receiver front. McVay said on Nov. 11 that Week 13 is a "realistic timeline" for Davante Adams to return from a ruptured hamstring he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6.

The Rams are on bye this week and will host the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve to kick off Week 12. Their Week 13 matchup is against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday Night Football.

Since falling to 2-4 after losing to the Cardinals, the Rams have won four straight games. Their 6-4 record is tied with the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks in the race for the final playoff spot in the NFC.

articles.title: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB Amid Possible Josh Johnson Start vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals may have to turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals may have to turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday that he is preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. However, LaFleur added that he is not yet ready to completely close the door on Beck starting, calling the back injury a "minute-by-minute thing."

After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice.

After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday.

The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times.

Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later.

Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action.

Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions.

Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record.

Regardless of who starts at quarterback, the 3-7 Cardinals are going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.

articles.title: Daniel Jones Released by Colts, Anthony Richardson to Take Over as QB1 After Surprise Move
articles.summary: In a stunning turn of events, the Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones following Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
In a stunning turn of events, the Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones following Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans.

Anthony Richardson will take over as the new starter, head coach Shane Steichen said on Friday.

The move comes just over eight months after Jones signed a two-year, $88 million contract to return to Indianapolis following a season-ending Achilles injury suffered in 2025. The deal represented the largest two-year contract in NFL history at the time.

The 2026 season quickly went off the rails for Jones and the Colts. Jones went 3-8 over 11 starts, completing just 58.4 percent of his passes for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and a league-leading 13 interceptions.

Richardson, the Colts' 2023 first-round draft pick, will now have six games to prove he's worthy of a longer look by the Colts or another team searching for a stopgap solution under center in 2027.

The Florida product owns a career record of 8-7. He's completed 50.6 percent of his passes for 2,408 yards, 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions while rushing for 640 yards and 10 touchdowns on 118 carries.

Richardson, whose fifth-year option was declined by the Colts, is set to become an unrestricted free agent in March.

articles.title: Daniel Jones released by Colts as Anthony Richardson Sr. takes over as starter
articles.summary: Richardson will start the Colts' next game at home against the Giants in Week 12.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Shane Steichen announced Friday. Anthony Richardson Sr. will take over as the team's starter going forward.

The decision comes after the Colts dropped to 3-8 on the season following Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans . Jones went 12-for-27 for 144 yards and one interception in the defeat and was benched late in the game. He has 13 interceptions this season and has been picked off in 10 of 11 games.

"Can't say enough good things about Daniel," Steichen said Thursday. "Just the ultimate competitor, ultimate teammate, the toughness that he brought to our football team."

Jones will now go on waivers and if he is not claimed will become a free agent Monday afternoon.

Jones originally joined the Colts via free agency in March 2025, signing a one-year, $14 million contract. He beat out Richardson for the starting job last season and went on to throw for the second-most yards (3,101) and touchdowns (19) in his career.

His 2025 season was cut short after an 8-2 start when he sustained a fibula fracture before later suffering an Achilles tear.

Last March, the Colts spent big and handed Jones (two years, $88 million) and leading receiver Alec Pierce (four years, $112 million) extensions, signaling a push to build off a strong start to 2025 before injuries derailed it all.

Jones and the Colts struggled in 2026 and the team went into "sell mode" before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. Over 11 games, Jones threw for 1,974 yards, 7 touchdowns and 13 interceptions, while being sacked 27 times.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Minnesota Vikings, Jones' former team, and the Baltimore Ravens, showed interest in acquiring the 29-year-old, but were turned down.

Anthony Richardson Sr.'s second chance at being QB1

Steichen said he will "evaluate everything" after the Texans loss. A day later, the decision was to move on from Jones and bring Richardson back into the starting job. It will be the 24-year-old's first start since 2024 and only his fifth appearance over the past two seasons.

Richardson, who threw for 1,814 yards and posted 8 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 2024, is getting one final chance to stick with the Colts. The team already declined his fifth-year option in April. The fourth overall pick in the 2023 draft had requested a move, but a trade partner was not found.

Now, with the Colts continuing to look toward 2027, the final six games of the season will serve as Richardson's tryout, even as a possible four-game suspension looms overhead following an October charge for possession of marijuana .

"I've just got to keep doing what I've been doing, coming in the building, showing up to work," Richardson said earlier this month . "Just preparing like I was going to be the starter regardless of what decision [Steichen] makes. I've just got to make sure I'm prepared when my number's called."

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Release Stuns NFL World As Jets Fans Celebrate Colts' Decision Amid Struggles
articles.summary: After the Indianapolis Colts suffered a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night, the team surprisingly released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday.
articles.body:
After the Indianapolis Colts suffered a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night, the team surprisingly released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday.

As the Colts now sit at 3-8, Anthony Richardson Sr. will serve as their starting quarterback moving forward.

Many were stunned by the decision after Indianapolis didn't trade Jones ahead of the deadline. The move was also celebrated by New York Jets fans, as the Jets own the Colts' 2027 first-round draft pick.

New York received Indianapolis' 2027 first-rounder as part of the Nov. 2025 trade that was headlined by star cornerback Sauce Gardner getting sent from the Jets to the Colts.

At the time, Indianapolis looked to capitalize on the momentum of the team's 7-2 start to the 2025 season as well as a breakout year from Jones.

The trade ultimately didn't propel the Colts to the playoffs, as they finished with an 8-9 record while Jones suffered a season-ending torn Achilles .

Although he was able to return for Week 1 this year, the 29-year-old struggled throughout Indianapolis' first 11 games. Jones completed a career-low 58.4 percent of his throws for 1,974 yards and seven touchdowns compared to 13 interceptions.

The Colts' slow start prompted them to sell at the deadline, trading away key pieces including left guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, wide receiver Josh Downs and veteran wideout Keenan Allen.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero previously reported that opposing front offices also called Indianapolis regarding Jones' availability, but the team "never had any intention of moving him."

In two games since the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Jones threw for a mere 252 yards and one touchdown while getting picked off three times before he was released.

articles.title: Drake Maye Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Severity, Latest Timeline for Patriots QB's Return
articles.summary: New details about the severity of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's leg injury have come to light.
articles.body:
New details about the severity of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's leg injury have come to light.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss , tests revealed Maye suffered a fractured right fibula that is expected to keep him out "deep into the regular season if he is able to return this year at all."

The report noted there is no ligament damage, nor will Maye require surgery.

Maye was injured on the opening possession of New England's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday when he was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson.

The Patriots star limped to the sideline and was later shown on the Fox broadcast walking back to the locker room.

It was initially reported the Patriots were concerned about Maye's ankle as they awaited test results, but the expectation has always been he would miss at least most of the remainder of the season.

One potential wrinkle to this situation, which Reiss and Schefter pointed out, is the Patriots only have one remaining IR return designation left to use this season.

Both Maye and AJ Brown, who is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, would be candidates to go on IR under normal circumstances.

The Patriots are still in playoff contention in the AFC with a 5-5 record. They are only one game behind the Cleveland Browns for the final wild card spot entering Week 11.

New England and Cleveland are on a bye this week, so the playoff positioning will not change. The Patriots' remaining schedule includes four games against winning teams, including the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos.

Tommy DeVito replaced Maye for the remainder of the Lions game. He went 12-of-24 for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

An undrafted free agent out of Illinois in 2023, DeVito has started eight games in his NFL career. He threw for 913 yards, seven touchdowns, one interception and completed 63.8 percent of his attempts in six starts with the New York Giants in 2023.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Injured, Latest NFL Rumors on Patriots WR's Hamstring and Timeline to Return
articles.summary: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is expected to miss "multiple weeks" due to a hamstring injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is expected to miss "multiple weeks" due to a hamstring injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss .

Brown suffered the injury during New England's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 10.

His early exit came in his return from a two-game absence due to knee issues .

Brown also had a stint on injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury during New England's Week 1 matchup with the Seattle Seahawks.

His health woes have been concerning, as the Patriots had high expectations for the three-time Pro Bowler after acquiring him in a blockbuster trade with the Philadelphia Eagles on June 1.

New England sent a 2028 first-round draft pick as well as a 2027 fifth-round selection to Philadelphia in exchange for Brown.

While the 29-year-old also experienced problems with availability near the end of his tenure on the Eagles, he still recorded at least 1,000 receiving yards and seven touchdown catches in every season from 2022-25.

This year, Brown has hauled in 11 receptions for 128 yards without being able to find the end zone across four games.

The Patriots have been hit hard by injuries this year while they've attempted to return to the Super Bowl, as quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury against Detroit that could sideline him for the remainder of the season.

New England currently sits at 5-5 during its Week 11 bye and is in serious danger of missing the playoffs if both Brown and Maye are forced to miss an extended period of time.
